input.title: Photo Production Assistant - Apparel
input.description: About Comfrt: Comfrt is one of the fastest-growing direct-to-consumer brands, dedicated to blending mental wellness, inclusivity, and elevated comfort into every piece we create. Our mission goes beyond clothing — we strive to build a community where everyone feels supported and seen. Role Overview: We are looking for a highly organized and detail-oriented Photo Production Assistant - Apparel to support the day-to-day operations of Comfrt's Miami studio. You will keep apparel samples organized and the studio running smoothly while providing hands-on support during photo production days—including setup, garment prep, and on-set logistics. This is an on-site role critical to ensuring our e-commerce and marketing photography goes off without a hitch. Key Responsibilities: Organize, catalog, and maintain inventory of all samples and production garments. Keep racks, shelves, and storage areas tidy, labeled, and logically organized at all times. Track all sample movement in and out of the studio for shoots, fittings, loans, and returns, ensuring accurate records are maintained. Perform quality control checks on garments prior to shoots, reviewing fit, construction, and cleanliness. Steam, tag, and prep all garments for content days and photo shoot days. Assist during fittings, photo shoots, and studio visits, including set-up, teardown, and on-set support throughout the day. Maintain overall studio cleanliness, including sweeping, tidying common areas, and managing supply levels. Proactively identify workflow improvements and stay ahead of studio needs before they become issues. Support miscellaneous errands, returns, and supply pickups as needed. Requirements: 2+ years of hands-on experience working in fashion/apparel photo production or photo studio environments, with proven experience supporting and prepping garments for photoshoots . Strong organizational and project management skills , with the ability to manage high-volume production workflows, timelines, and multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Experience with e-commerce, fashion, or apparel photography/production strongly preferred , with a professional understanding of studio and shoot processes. Exceptional organizational skills and a strong attention to detail. Experience with garment steaming, care, and quality inspection. Familiarity with sample tracking systems or inventory management tools. An eye for visual organization and brand presentation. Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously in a fast-paced environment without losing accuracy. A proactive, low-ego attitude. You take initiative, no task is too small, and you take pride in keeping things running smoothly. Strong communication skills and comfort working closely with a small, collaborative team. Physically able to stand for extended periods, lift garment racks, and handle the physical demands of an active studio environment. Based in Miami, FL . This role requires full-time, on-site presence. Must have own means of transportation Why Join Comfrt? Be part of a purpose-driven company that’s shaping the future of comfort and mental wellness. Work in a supportive, creative environment where your ideas and growth are valued. Enjoy Comfrt benefits such as generous paid time off, company-covered health insurance, 5% 401k match, and discounts on all Comfrt products! Comfrt is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

input.title: Media Management Operations Specialist
input.description: This is a project/limited term position, unless otherwise amended or terminated as deliverables within this project are completed. The Media Management Operations Specialist is a specialized, hands-on technical role responsible for the processing, management, quality control, organization, storage, and lifecycle of media assets supporting network broadcast, sports, news, and production operations. Job Duties: Execute and monitor media ingest, transcoding, transfer, QC, archive, restoration, export, and distribution workflows across broadcast, post-production, and cloud-based environments. Manage and organize media within MAM, AVID, Cloud systems, archive, and shared-storage systems, ensuring assets are properly processed, organized, accessible, and available within required deadlines. Perform comprehensive technical and visual quality control (QC) of media, identifying issues involving video, audio, timecode, resolution, frame rate, synchronization, file integrity, metadata, and technical specifications. Validate metadata, naming conventions, folder structures, media placement, and delivery specifications to ensure accuracy and compliance with established standards. Monitor media storage, asset availability, retention, archive, and restoration activities in support of content lifecycle and storage-management requirements. Independently troubleshoot failed or delayed ingest, transcode, transfer, archive, restoration, and delivery workflows and perform appropriate first-level corrective actions. Analyze workflow failures, identify potential points of failure, gather relevant technical information, and provide detailed escalations to Engineering, Media Systems, and other technical teams when required. Support time-sensitive media requirements for live events, sports, digital streaming, broadcast, and production operations. Maintain accurate operational documentation and clearly communicate workflow status, technical discrepancies, risks, and escalations to appropriate stakeholders. Identify opportunities to improve media-management processes, operational efficiency, and workflow reliability. Collaborate with Media Operations, Sports Operations, Production, Editorial, Engineering, Media Systems, and other technical teams to resolve issues and meet critical production deadlines. Adapts to fluctuating schedules, including nights, overnights, weekends, and holidays, in a high-demand, fast-paced environment. Works under the direct supervision of the Sr Manager of Media Operations and is responsible for completing any other tasks as assigned by the manager. Basic Requirements: Minimum 5 years of experience in a production, postproduction, broadcast, or communications environment Fluency in English & Spanish Strong technical knowledge of broadcast media management and post-production workflows, including ingest, transcoding, QC, media movement, storage management, archive, restoration, distribution, and content lifecycle management. Demonstrated proficiency with professional MAM and AVID environments, including AVID Media Composer, Interplay, Media Central Cloud UX, Media Shuttle, or comparable broadcast and post-production platforms. Strong knowledge of professional video formats, codecs, resolutions, frame rates, and media specifications, including HD, UHD/4K, MXF, MOV, MP4, Apple ProRes, XAVC, and proxy media. Strong understanding of cloud-based broadcast and post-production environments, including Microsoft Azure or comparable cloud technologies and the integration of cloud and on-premises media workflows. Demonstrated expertise in technical and visual media QC, including the ability to identify and assess video, audio, timecode, synchronization, metadata, file-integrity, and specification-related issues. Strong knowledge of media storage, metadata management, naming conventions, folder structures, asset organization, retention, archive, and restoration principles. Demonstrated ability to independently troubleshoot media workflow failures, identify probable causes, perform initial corrective actions, and determine when technical escalation is required. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with an understanding of workflow dependencies and downstream impacts across editorial, production, distribution, and broadcast operations. Ability to interpret technical specifications and media delivery requirements and ensure assets meet established technical and operational standards. Ability to independently prioritize and manage multiple high-volume, time-sensitive workflows while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly communicate technical issues to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to quickly learn and develop proficiency in new broadcast, post-production, MAM, cloud, and media-management technologies. Desired Characteristics: Bachelor’s or 2-year degree in Communications or Media preferred Experience in international broadcast operations or media. Familiarity with broadcast and digital streaming media workflows. Exceptional time management, facilitation, and organizational skills Self-starter who exhibits ownership on assigned tasks and who will push for solutions that solve immediate problems while building towards long-term goals Ability to multitask and work in a fast paced, dead-line driven environment Accustomed to working in a team and collaborating with all levels within the organization Demonstrates strong attention to detail Ability to build rapport with clients and manage expectations Ability to effectively be flexible in approach, and respond well to pressure Additional Requirements: This position is required to be performed on onsite from an NBCUniversal-designated worksite.  Must be willing to work in the greater Miami, Florida area Willingness to travel with short notice and on weekends Must be 18 years or older Must be willing to work flexible hours including late and/or last-minute scheduling changes in a 24/7 production work environment Must be available to work (whenever necessary for show production) early mornings, evenings, overnights, holidays and weekends Must have unrestricted work authorization to work in the United States. input.description: We are hiring a Head of Marketing & Communications to tell the garden3d story across the internet, from wherever in the world you happen to be. More details if you check our original job posting link About garden3d We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions. Our client roster includes Google , Stripe , Figma , Hinge , Black Socialists in America , ACLU , Pratt , Parsons , Mozilla , The Nobel Prize , MIT , Gnosis , Etsy & Gagosian . We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill , and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space . We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs. Sanctuary Computer — Development At Sanctuary Computer we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson. Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development. XXIX — Design When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be. We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility. Index Space — Community A network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools. We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care. garden3d TK — Media At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture. We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music. Plus, our partner organizations https://www.thelightphone.com/ https://www.mill.com/ https://www.ingredient-ai.com/ The Head of Marketing & Communications Role The garden3d Head of Marketing & Communications has one mandate: make sure everything we put on the internet is compelling and interesting. garden3d is a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and each needs its own voice, its own audience, and its own drumbeat of work worth sharing. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis , this person decides what we make, where it runs, and whether it clears our bar. You can be based anywhere. A lot of our studios, spaces and people gravitate around New York, so there's some pull to be here, and a good part of this job is noticing what's happening in our world and turning it into content. But we already work across timezones, and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you. This role will interface with studio leads, designers, developers, editors, animators, photographers, community managers, event producers and ad platforms across every garden3d vertical. Simply, this person can easily context shift between our massively diverse set of workstreams, find the most compelling stories, and get them produced at an exceedingly high bar. This person owns our channels end to end: the garden3d Substack , our podcast, Instagram, X, and the paid accounts behind them. They collab with our team, and a rotating cast of freelance editors, designers and animators, and they run the calendar that keeps a dozen workstreams shipping on time. They think in PESO terms (paid, earned, shared, owned) with the weight on shared and owned media - paid is a tool they use deliberately, and traditional press is a bonus, but not generally where we focus. The ambition runs past marketing a services business. garden3d TK is our young experimental media company, and this role is its engine: books, screenplays, music, media, activations: a record label for ideas. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, a network of community spaces and an open P&L and sees the best content brief on the internet. Responsibilities & Mandates ‍ Quality never less than 8/10 We aspire for 10/10, celebrate 9/10 and never publish anything that’s not an 8/10 - visually, narratively, and in production quality. This person holds that bar across every post, video, essay and episode on every vertical, and would rather kill a piece than let a 6 out the door. Their feedback makes work better and faster, without micromanaging the people who make it. Social That Stops the Scroll They carry a current, practitioner-level read on how each platform works right now: what arrests someone mid-scroll, how a hook earns the next three seconds, why a format lands on TikTok and dies on LinkedIn. Short-form video is a first-class craft here, not an afterthought. ️ A House of Brands, Each in Its Own Voice Sanctuary Computer doesn't sound like XXIX, and neither sounds like Index. They manage several messaging columns at once, keeping each brand's tone distinct while the umbrella story stays coherent. Case Study Production Every client engagement across our creative agencies should end in a case study worth reading. They own that production line - interviewing the team, shaping the narrative, art-directing the assets - and ship case studies that win each studio its next project. ️ Websites That Put Our Best Foot Forward Our websites are usually the first place a prospective client or hire meets us. They own the strategy behind every garden3d site - what it says, what work it shows, and how clearly it communicates what each studio can do - and they keep sites, decks and other collateral current as the work moves, so what people find is sharp and true. ️ Editorial Ownership The Substack , the podcast, and our transparency publications (like the open-source P&L we release every year) are theirs to run: the calendar, the standards, the growth. They capture what happens in our spaces - Index, USB Club, and the communities around them - and turn it into work worth sharing. Producing, Paid & Distribution They direct producers, editors and freelancers like a showrunner: briefs are clear, deadlines are real, and many workstreams move at once without dropping quality. They run paid spend on Meta, Instagram and wherever our audiences live - building audiences, running A/B/C tests on both narrative and adset, and owning budgets against results they can show. Data-Driven Reporting & ROI They measure what our content actually does - audience growth, engagement, leads, pipeline influenced - and report on it plainly. Paid spend, organic effort and production time all get judged on return, and next quarter's plan follows the numbers. Presence IRL garden3d shows up in person: events, conferences, talks, Index programming, and the dinners and openings where our world gathers. They decide which touchpoints are worth our time, get us there looking like ourselves, and bring back stories worth publishing. Culture They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The producers and creatives they direct do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is real, and the taste rubs off. Special Projects In addition to day to day responsibilities, here’s an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years Turning garden3d TK into a real experimental media brand: books, screenplays, music, and shows Growing our podcast into a property with its own audience Launch campaigns for new Index spaces, USB Club drops, and community programs Making our annual open-source P&L release a media moment Standing up a small content studio that serves all four studios' new-business pipelines Building the systems (and hiring the people) that let us publish more often, while aspiring for a 10/10 content, and never dropping below an 8/10 Qualifications This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills: Must have: 8+ years in marketing, content or brand leadership, with real time inside creative studios, agencies or founder-led companies A portfolio that proves exceptional taste - visual, narrative, and tone of voice A design background and/or fluency & comfort producing own visual assets at the required quality level in Figma when necessary Experience owning a company's web presence: site strategy, messaging, and keeping capabilities collateral current Exceptional project management: content calendars, production pipelines, many workstreams at once Short-form video fluency: they've shipped work for Reels, TikTok and Shorts and can say why each piece performed Extensive experience & comfort managing creatives & producers (editors, designers, animators, freelancers) and getting better work out of them than they'd make alone Hands-on experience running paid social on Meta, Instagram and other platforms: audience building, budget ownership, and A/B/C testing across narrative and ad set Working fluency in the PESO model, with a point of view on where paid, earned, shared and owned media each earn their keep Nice-to-have: Experience producing a brand's IRL presence: events, conferences, talks, and the follow-through that turns them into content Podcast or audio production experience Comfort/experience managing multiple messaging columns in a house of brands Newsletter growth experience, Substack especially Community & events marketing: programming, launches, IRL moments Photography, motion or editing chops of their own Fluency with AI production tools, plus the judgment to know when not to use them A press & media network (traditional PR isn't the focus, but relationships help) Experience marketing to design & engineering decision-makers at companies like our clients Book publishing or long-form media experience Experience growing a services business's story into a consumer-scale audience Who you are The person we’re looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. They’re flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work “smart” by carefully managing their workflow and team. How we interview After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests. From there, we’ll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where we’re going as a business. For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow. Compensation This role greatly favors autonomous, competent & ambitious operators. It will begin with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between $75 - $120 p/hr pending seniority & experience. In the first few weeks of the trial, this individual will propose their own goals to define success in their trial, and present them to our leadership team for approval. At garden3d, we believe that those who shoulder the most responsibility and create the greatest impact should be paid accordingly. If this individual exceeds expectations by the end of the 4-month period, we'll shape a permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as our audiences and revenue do. Finally, after a period of proven success in this role (12 - 24 months), this individual will become eligible to join our worker ownership program. ‍ How we work: We believe that there’s a better balance between the poles of freelancing & full time, and for that reason we work differently to most shops: Transparency & Ownership: We release out Profit & Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business & money with everyone in the company. We’re proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team & community. 150% Carbon Negative: ** Our studio offsets 150% of the carbon we use to do business each year, dated back to our founding in 2015. We turn down work that is not in-line with our morals, and we encourage our peers to do the same. We have been certified climate neutral since 2021 . Strong Morals: ** Since our founding, we've turned down somewhere between $1mm - $2mm of work that didn't meet our moral standards. (Most of that was DTC brands that can't show a valid sustainability initiative). Async & Decentralized: We use tools optimized for calm, thoughtful communication, and opt for async whenever possible. We fight hard to maintain our focus time. Remote Friendly: Our company is fluent in remote work, making our workplace more decentralized, and democratized in the process. Ideas & Products: In our spare studio time, we work to build our own open source or internal products to diversify & bolster our income. We create amazing technology products for our clients, so why not for the studio? → Read more on our Substack, over here . Kindly submit a complete and thoughtful application, including relevant links that help verify your work experience and identity. Applications with missing or insufficient information will not move forward in the review process. Our team carefully reviews every complete submission, and we truly appreciate the time and effort you put into applying! We’re excited to hear from you! ❤

input.description: WHO ARE WE? Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz , All About Cookies , and OnlyInYourState . We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies. Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment. We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries. WHY JOIN US? You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato . BASE SALARY: $80,000 to $115,000 per year, paid semi-monthly The Role Launch Potato’s sales and partnerships team spends a lot of time on the road. Over the next twelve months, we expect to attend roughly 26 external conferences and trade shows, with the busiest stretch falling between August and October. We’re looking for someone to take ownership of that program and make sure every event is thoughtfully planned, well organized, and set up to drive real business outcomes. You’ll own the external event calendar end to end for our revenue teams: helping determine which shows we attend, coordinating who goes, managing logistics and travel, preparing materials, supporting meeting planning, and making sure follow-up happens after the event. This role is less about large-scale brand activations and more about making our conference strategy run exceptionally well. Success looks like sellers arriving prepared, calendars full of the right meetings, materials ready, logistics handled, and clear next steps coming out of every show. You’ll work closely with senior leaders across the business, including the CRO, and have the opportunity to turn what is currently a highly manual process into a more scalable and repeatable event program. It’s a great fit for someone who enjoys being organized, moving quickly, working cross-functionally, and owning the details that make a high-performing commercial team more effective. Why This Seat You work directly with the CRO. Not through three layers. You will sit in the revenue conversation and see how deals actually get made. Real ownership from day one. The program exists but the system does not. You get to build it. Visible impact. Your work shows up as booked meetings and closed partnerships, not as a slide in someone else's deck. You will not be doing this alone. Judy runs our on-site logistics at HQ and is genuinely great at it. She is your partner on assets, swag, and shipping, not a resource you task out. Room to grow into more. As the business grows and we take on bigger activations, this seat grows with it. What You'll Own The show calendar Own the annual trade show and conference calendar, including which shows we attend and why Bring recommendations to the CRO rather than waiting to be asked which shows matter Work backward from each show: passes, deadlines, sponsorships, booth space, speaking slots Build the 2027 calendar before the deadlines build it for us Making the team ready Chase the team for who is attending, by when, and make the call visible early Keep the CRO ahead of every deadline, so he reacts instead of remembering Coordinate with the design team on collateral, one-pagers, and sales assets, and project manage them to the date Partner with Judy on swag, samples, and shipping so the right materials arrive in the right city On site, for the shows that need it Attend roughly five shows a year where we exhibit, host a dinner, or run executive meetings Run the logistics on those so the sellers sell and nobody is cutting name tags an hour before the door opens Be the go-to for the team when something breaks on the ground, whether or not you are there The money and the mechanics Track and manage the event budget, and flag overruns before they happen Own month-end reconciliation with Finance and answer the questions before they get asked Help us move onto a modern travel and expense platform, then run the program on it Build the small activations that deepen partner relationships: a dinner, a golf outing, the thing a partner actually wants What You'll Bring 3+ years running events, trade shows, or field programs in support of a sales, partnerships, or business development team Direct experience owning a conference or trade show end to end, including vendor negotiation, booth or sponsorship contracts, and a budget you were accountable for A track record of chasing people down and getting an answer, warmly and without needing permission Comfort working remotely with a team that is spread out and moving fast Strong written communication, because most of this job is written and most of it is asynchronous Real curiosity about AI tools and how to use them to do more than the job technically requires Nice to Have Experience in performance marketing, affiliate, adtech, fintech, or digital media You have run a program on a travel, expense, or event platform such as Ramp, Brex, Navan, TripActions, Cvent, or Concur, and have an opinion about what works Experience helping select or roll out one of those platforms Existing relationships with conference organizers in our space What Great Looks Like In 90 days: you know the calendar cold, the next three shows are fully handled, and our Co-founder & CRO have stopped tracking event deadlines. In six months: the 2027 calendar is built and budgeted. Sellers come to you with which shows they want, and you bring the recommendation up. Finance stops chasing event expenses because reconciliation is clean. In a year: the program runs on a system rather than in someone's head. You are proposing the small activations that win partners, not just executing the ones you were handed. This Isn't the Right Seat If You Want to design large brand activations and experiential campaigns. We do small and targeted, deliberately. Need someone to tell you what to do next. Most of this job is noticing what is about to fall over. Are looking for a step toward people management in the next year or two. This is an individual contributor seat. Prefer to work through a defined process someone else built. You are building the process. Total Compensation Base salary is set according to market rates for the nearest major metro and varies based on Launch Potato’s Levels Framework. Launch Potato is a performance-driven company, which means once you are hired, future increases will be based on company and personal performance, not annual cost of living adjustments. input.title: Strategic Content Editor (Contract-to-Hire)

organization.name: REGEX SEO
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: The situation, honestly Our content department head is going on a planned leave in the near future. Before that happens, we need a senior editor in place who can hold the line on strategy and quality while she's out, then keep raising the bar when she's back. This starts as a contract role with a clear path to a full-time hire based on performance . We're not being coy about it: the leave is the reason for the speed, and the contract period is a working trial on both sides. If you do well, there's a permanent senior seat here with a benefits package. Because of that timeline, we need someone who can ramp fast and operate independently. You'll get a real onboarding, documented strategy, and a team that knows what it's doing. You will not get six months to find your footing. Who we are RGX is a digital marketing agency built for home service businesses: HVAC, pest control, plumbing, electrical, and the trades that keep homes running. Our clients are not hobby businesses. They’re doing $1.5M+ in annual revenue, investing in growth. We help serious service businesses get clearer about what they offer, sharper about who they serve, and more direct about why a customer should choose them. Strategy first. Every sentence accountable to the business it serves. What you'll actually do Review strategy before content exists. You'll read content briefs, keyword strategies, and funnel plans before writing starts, and pressure-test them. If the targeting is off, the search intent is misread, or the funnel logic doesn't hold, you catch it at the brief stage, not the draft stage. Edit for strategic alignment. Every draft gets checked against the strategy it was written to serve. You'll verify the copy matches the persona, the CTA fits the funnel stage, and the content actually satisfies the search intent we're targeting. Create editing standards where they don't exist. If you notice a recurring writing problem, a missing tone of voice guide, or a gap in our editorial process, you build the fix. You don't wait to be asked, and you don't file it as someone else's problem. You do pause long enough to get leadership and team buy-in, because a standard only works if the people using it helped shape it. Fix what's broken, and fix it with the team rather than around them. Spot ranking opportunities the brief missed. You read SERPs, not just drafts. If a piece could capture a featured snippet with a structural change, or a related keyword cluster is sitting there unclaimed, you flag it and adjust. Run quality control. You're the last set of eyes before content ships. Clarity, flow, tone, accuracy, brand voice, and the unglamorous stuff like internal links, metadata, and formatting. You'll help formalize our QA process so quality doesn't depend on any one person being in the room. Give writers feedback that makes them better. Direct, specific, actionable notes that explain the strategic reasoning, not just the correction. Our writers are good. Your job is to make them sharper. Requirements Where this goes This role exists because our content department is growing faster than one director can quality-control. The interim coverage is the immediate need. The real opportunity is what comes after. The person who succeeds here will help build the editorial function itself: the standards, the QA program, the feedback systems that let a team scale without quality slipping. As the department grows, this seat is positioned to grow into a leadership role, including mentoring and eventually managing editors. You'll be learning team leadership directly from the content director, with real responsibility from week one rather than a title and a waiting period. If you're a senior editor who has hit the ceiling at your current job, this is the next rung. Who does well in this role 5+ years editing strategic marketing content (SEO content, landing pages, email, PPC assets) in an agency or similar fast-moving environment. You've edited for performance outcomes, not just polish. You can read an SEO strategy document and find its weak points. Keyword selection, intent mapping, funnel logic, content architecture. This is fluency, not familiarity. You work independently by default. During the leave period, you'll be making editorial calls without a director to escalate to. You need the judgment to make those calls and the documentation habits to make them defensible. You're a genuine team player. Independent doesn't mean lone wolf. You'll be collaborating daily with writers, strategists, and PMs, and your feedback style needs to build trust fast. You're direct and kind in the same sentence. Writers should leave your edits better at their jobs, not deflated. You want more responsibility than your current role gives you. You've probably already been doing unofficial leadership work: mentoring writers, building processes nobody asked for, being the person the team actually goes to. You want a seat where that's the job description instead of the extra credit. Benefits How the role works Contract engagement to start, with conversion to full-time based on performance during the contract period. Fully remote. We'll need meaningful overlap with US Eastern Time business hours for collaboration. Competitive contract rate commensurate with experience ($3,000-$5,000 a month). Full-time conversion includes salary, benefits, PTO, and professional development budget. Originally posted on Himalayas

input.title: Content Editor, SEO & GEO

organization.name: Interdependence Public Relations
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: WHO WE ARE The PR industry hasn't really changed in fifty years. Relationships, lunches, luck, and a clip report at the end of the month. Interdependence is rebuilding it from the ground up. Interviewed, our proprietary platform, analyzes 300,000+ stories every day across a network of 250,000 journalists. We turn earned media into something measurable, repeatable, and worth paying for — and apply the same data and discipline across paid, social, content, and brand. Integrated marketing run by one team, on one system, accountable to one result. Forbes named us one of America's Best PR Agencies. Our 100+ person team works with brands, CMOs, founders, and entrepreneurs across consumer, healthcare, tech, B2B, travel and entertainment. We move fast. The best argument wins. We hire for sharp thinking, real craft, and ownership from day one. If you want comfortable, this isn't the place. If you want to win, build with us. THE ROLE We are looking for a sharp, experienced Content Editor to help shape content used across SEO, Generative Engine Optimization, PR, content marketing, reputation management and brand campaigns. A large part of this role involves taking AI-generated content and making it genuinely publication-ready.That means much more than proofreading. You will be expected to recognize weak writing, repetitive ideas, questionable claims, poor sourcing and content that simply does not accomplish what it is supposed to do. Sometimes that will mean making a few edits. Other times it will mean restructuring a section or rewriting it completely. The ideal candidate is an excellent editor, a strong researcher and someone who knows when not to trust the first answer AI provides. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Edit, rewrite and improve AI-generated content for client websites and third-party publications Turn rough or generic AI content into clear, natural and useful writing Research unfamiliar topics and verify facts, statistics, claims and sources Identify AI hallucinations, unsupported claims and questionable citations Remove repetitive, generic or overly formulaic AI writing Improve article structure, flow, readability and organization Optimize content around keywords, topics and search intent Structure information so it can be easily understood by users, search engines and AI platforms Edit website content, blog articles, resource content, contributed articles and thought leadership pieces Adapt writing for different brands, industries and audiences Make sure content aligns with client messaging and positioning Review titles, headings, meta descriptions, links and anchor text when needed Identify language that could create factual, reputational or brand concerns Work closely with SEO, GEO, PR and account teams Manage multiple assignments and deadlines across different client accounts QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of professional writing, editing, journalism, content marketing or digital marketing experience Excellent editing, rewriting, proofreading and grammar skills Strong research and fact-checking ability Experience working with AI-generated content Ability to recognize when content needs more than surface-level editing Working knowledge of SEO and search intent Ability to quickly understand and edit content across different industries Strong attention to detail Excellent organizational and time-management skills Experience using generative AI platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini A specific college degree is not required. Strong editing skills, sound judgment and relevant experience are much more important to us. NICE TO HAVES Agency experience SEO content experience GEO, AEO or AI search experience PR or earned media experience Experience with reputation or brand management Experience editing content for third-party publications WordPress or CMS experience Familiarity with Google Search Console, Semrush, Ahrefs, Moz or similar platforms Basic familiarity with schema markup Familiarity with AP style YOU SHOULD APPLY IF... You read AI-generated content and immediately notice what is wrong with it. You can tell when a paragraph sounds polished but does not actually say anything useful. You question statistics and claims before accepting them. You know the difference between a credible source and a weak one. You are comfortable deleting an entire section and starting over when that is the best editorial decision. You can take a complicated topic, research it quickly and make the content understandable without pretending to be the subject matter expert. You understand that good digital content needs to work for the reader first while also supporting search, AI visibility, brand positioning and broader marketing goals. ABOUT GEO: Previous Generative Engine Optimization experience is a plus but it is not required. GEO is an emerging area of digital marketing focused on improving how brands, companies and information are understood, surfaced and cited by AI-driven search and answer platforms. We can teach our GEO methodology. What is much harder to teach is strong editorial judgment, research ability and the instinct to recognize when content simply is not good enough. That is what we are looking for. HIRING PROCESS Candidates may be asked to provide relevant writing or editing samples. Final candidates should also expect a practical editing exercise involving AI-generated content. We are interested in seeing not only how well you edit but what you identify as needing to be changed and why. WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING AT INTERDEPENDENCE 🏡 100% Remote, Forever - Work from anywhere in the U.S. while enjoying the flexibility of a fully remote workplace. Skip the commute, create a workspace that works for you, and collaborate with teammates across the country, all without sacrificing connection or career growth. 🩺 Comprehensive Health Benefits - Choose from three Anthem Blue Cross PPO medical plans, plus dental and vision coverage to support your health and well-being. 💰 Retirement Savings - Save for the future with our 401(k) program, including a company match that is increasing to 3% by 2027 . 🌴 Work-Life Balance - Enjoy paid vacation, sick time, 11 company holidays, a floating holiday, and Summer Fridays to recharge and spend more time doing what you love. 👶 Paid Maternity Leave - We support growing families with paid maternity leave, giving new moms dedicated time to recover, bond with their baby, and return to work with confidence. 📈 Career Growth - As one of the nation's fastest-growing PR and strategic communications firms, we're committed to helping ambitious people grow. Take on meaningful challenges, develop new skills, lead from every level, and build a career with real impact. 🌟 Supportive, Collaborative Culture - We set high standards, celebrate big wins, and work together to achieve exceptional results. You'll join a team that's collaborative, entrepreneurial, and committed to helping one another succeed. Originally posted on Himalayas

Whether you work in one of our regions, are an accountant at the national office or a specialist in our Information Resource Center, you work each day on making our bold goal a reality: to enable patients with blood cancer to gain more than one million years of life by 2040. Summary: The Manager, Social Media: Partnerships leads social media strategy and activation for national partnerships, corporate collaborations, sponsorship activations, and partner campaigns. This role serves as the primary social media lead for partnership marketing and activation efforts, responsible for maximizing partner visibility, audience engagement, brand awareness, revenue generation, and campaign impact across Blood Cancer United's social channels while ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and brand standards. Reporting to the Sr. Manager, Social Media, this position serves as the primary social media partner to the Business Development and Healthcare Partnership Activation teams and the Sr. Marketing Manager, Corporate Partnerships, collaborating to develop and execute social strategies that support partner objectives and organizational goals. The role also works closely with stakeholders across Marketing, Mission, Development, Regional, and Communications teams, as well as agency partners and external organizations, to support mission-focused initiatives, fundraising campaigns, revenue-generating opportunities, and key organizational priorities through integrated social media programs. Core Responsibilities / Primary Duties Social Media Strategy & Partnership Activations Primary Duty 1: Lead Partnership Social Strategy Develop and execute social media strategies supporting national partnerships, sponsorship activations, corporate collaborations, and partner-focused campaigns. Serve as the primary social media lead for partnership activations, ensuring alignment with campaign objectives, organizational priorities, and brand standards. Identify opportunities to leverage strategic partnerships and collaborations to expand reach, increase engagement, and amplify mission-driven storytelling. Develop social toolkits, messaging guidance, and amplification strategies that help partners effectively support organizational objectives while maintaining brand integrity. Primary Duty 2: Manage Partnership Planning & Execution Lead social media planning and activation for partnership campaigns across Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, X, Threads, Bluesky, YouTube, and emerging platforms. Primary Duty 3: Collaborate Across Organizational Priorities Serve as the primary social media partner to the Business Development and Healthcare Partnership Activation teams, supporting partnership strategy, campaign development, and activation planning. Work closely with the Sr. Manager, Social Media to align partnership activations with organizational goals, mission priorities, fundraising efforts, and revenue-generating initiatives. Participate in enterprise content planning and prioritization efforts to ensure partnership activities support broader organizational campaigns and awareness moments. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Expertise across Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, X, Threads, Bluesky, YouTube, and emerging social platforms. input.description: Contract eLearning Visual Designer and Absorb LMS Producer Transforming approved course content into polished, engaging digital learning experiences Primary Point of Contact: Water's Edge HR Director (Internal Course Manager) Course Authorization and Prioritization: Water's Edge HR Director (Internal Course Manager) Classification: Independent Contractor Schedule: Flexible; hours will vary according to approved project workload and organizational priorities Location: Remote, with on-site work as needed for collaboration, photography, video, or audio production Contract Duration: October 2026-May 2027 Estimated Hours: To be determined based on approved course inventory Position Summary Central Church / Water's Edge is seeking a creative, technically capable, and highly organized Contract eLearning Visual Designer and Absorb LMS Producer to turn approved course content into clear, visually compelling, and easy-to-navigate learning experiences in the Absorb Learning Management System (LMS). This is a design and production role, not a course-writing role. Approved Course Content Writers and subject matter experts will supply the course purpose, learning objectives, written content, assessment content, and intended sequence. The contractor will determine how that approved material is best presented visually and technically inside Absorb, while preserving the writer's meaning, voice, and desired learner journey. The role may include graphic design, page and lesson design, multimedia production, video recording and editing, audio capture and cleanup, and the creation of reusable course templates and visual assets. The contractor will collaborate closely with course writers and the Internal Course Manager, but will not decide whether a course should be developed. Course authorization, sequencing within the organizational training portfolio, and project priority remain with the Water's Edge HR Director. Role Scope and Decision Rights The Water's Edge HR Director, serving as Internal Course Manager, authorizes new courses, establishes organizational priority, and identifies the accountable course owner. Approved Course Content Writers and subject matter experts are responsible for the substance of the course, including learning objectives, written copy, theological or policy accuracy, assessments, and required resources. The contractor is responsible for the visual treatment, media production, learner-facing presentation, and technical assembly of approved content in Absorb, subject to review and approval. In this role, the Water's Edge HR Director serves as the primary operational contact, coordinates access and platform standards, and supports final testing and publication workflows. Key Deliverables Visual Learning Design and Absorb Production Build and format approved Online Courses in Absorb LMS and, if licensed and selected for a project, Absorb Create. Translate approved Word, Google Docs, Pages, presentation, video, audio, and other source materials into polished digital learning experiences without rewriting or materially changing the content. Create a coherent visual system for each course, including course thumbnails, course posters, title treatments, chapter and lesson graphics, icons, diagrams, infographics, supporting images, downloadable resources, and video poster frames. Organize approved content into the chapters, Lessons, Learning Objects, and course sequence specified by the course writer, using sound visual hierarchy, pacing, and navigation to support the intended learning flow. Use layout, typography, color, imagery, motion, and interaction consistently so learners can easily understand where they are, what matters, and what to do next. Build or import interactive elements, knowledge checks, quizzes, and assessments from questions and answer logic supplied and approved by the course writer. Prepare and upload web-optimized graphics, documents, audio, video, and SCORM-compatible packages when a project calls for them. Video, Audio, and Multimedia Production Plan the visual and technical production approach for approved video or audio segments in collaboration with the course writer and project owner. Capture high-quality video and audio on site or remotely, including appropriate camera framing, lighting, composition, microphone selection, room setup, and recording quality. Edit video and audio for clarity and engagement, including color correction, audio cleanup and leveling, titles, lower thirds, motion graphics, transitions, music where approved, captions, and final compression for web delivery. Create screen recordings, demonstrations, voiceover-supported sequences, or other multimedia components when they improve the presentation of approved content. Maintain visual and audio consistency across lessons and courses, including reusable intros, outros, graphic packages, and export settings. Course Flow, Usability, and Quality Assurance Implement the course writer's intended flow and recommend visual, pacing, or navigation improvements when they would make the approved content easier to follow; obtain approval before changing sequence, wording, learning objectives, or assessment meaning. Configure and test learner-facing elements such as lesson order, completion behavior, buttons, links, downloads, embedded media, assessments, and navigation before publication. Test courses in both administrator and learner views, and on appropriate desktop, tablet, and mobile screen sizes. Apply practical accessibility standards to the visual build, including readable contrast and type size, descriptive alternative text, captions for video, clear headings, keyboard-friendly interactions where supported, and accessible downloadable resources. Identify and resolve visual, functional, media-playback, or responsive-design issues before final review. Brand, Templates, and Asset Management Ensure each course reflects the appropriate Central Church or Water's Edge brand, visual identity, audience, and ministry context. Develop and maintain reusable course templates, graphic systems, production checklists, and media standards that create consistency while allowing appropriate variation between course types and audiences. Maintain organized source and final files for graphics, video, audio, captions, downloadable resources, and course packages, using agreed naming and version-control practices. Design assets so future updates can be made efficiently by authorized staff or contractors. Collaboration and Project Management Receive assignments only after the Water's Edge HR Director, serving as Internal Course Manager, has authorized and prioritized the course. Partner with the Internal Course Manager, Approved Course Content Writers, subject matter experts, and other stakeholders to confirm the audience, approved source materials, desired learner experience, deliverables, timeline, review points, and acceptance criteria. Develop a visual concept or prototype when appropriate and secure direction before completing a full course build. Manage multiple approved projects from intake through design, production, review, revision, testing, and publication readiness. Estimate effort, track time and deliverables by project, and provide regular visibility into completed work, work in progress, upcoming decisions, and risks to schedule. Proactively identify missing assets, conflicting instructions, technical limitations, or dependencies and route them to the appropriate course writer or Internal Course Manager rather than making unapproved content decisions. Incorporate feedback accurately and deliver polished work within agreed timelines and review cycles. This Role Is Not Responsible For Deciding whether a course should be created, when it should be prioritized, or who should be required to complete it. Writing the substantive course content, defining the curriculum, establishing learning objectives, creating theological or policy positions, or serving as the subject matter expert. Changing approved copy, learning objectives, course sequence, or assessment meaning without the course writer's approval. Giving final approval for policy, legal, theological, ministry, or compliance accuracy. Publishing a course as final or assigning it to learners without the authorization required by the Internal Course Manager and the established LMS publication process. Ongoing learner administration, enrollment management, reporting, or LMS governance unless those duties are separately assigned in writing for a specific project. Qualifications Required A portfolio demonstrating strong visual design for digital learning, web content, multimedia, presentations, or comparable learner-facing experiences. Proficiency with relevant Adobe Creative Cloud applications, such as Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere Pro, After Effects, and/or Audition, with the ability to select the right tool for the work. Demonstrated ability to transform supplied content into an attractive, coherent, and intuitive visual experience without assuming authorship of the content itself. Practical video-production capability, including camera operation, lighting, composition, high-quality audio capture, editing, audio cleanup, captioning, and web-ready export. Strong understanding of typography, layout, image selection, visual hierarchy, pacing, brand consistency, and responsive digital design. Strong project and time-management skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, stakeholders, and review cycles. Clear communication, reliable follow-through, receptiveness to feedback, and excellent attention to detail. Ability to work independently while knowing when a content, priority, or approval decision must be returned to the responsible owner. Preferred Experience administering or building courses in Absorb LMS and/or Absorb Create. Experience with eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Storyline, Rise, Adobe Captivate, Camtasia, or comparable platforms. Familiarity with chapters, Lessons, Learning Objects, course posters, video poster images, Curricula, assessments, and completion settings in an LMS environment. Working knowledge of SCORM, xAPI, HTML5 course delivery, media optimization, and common browser or device compatibility issues. Knowledge of accessibility practices for digital learning, including captions, alternative text, color contrast, readable layouts, and WCAG-informed design. Experience producing training for staff, volunteers, members, customers, or other mixed internal and external audiences. Experience in a nonprofit, ministry, church, or multi-location organization is helpful but not required. What Success Looks Like The successful contractor will establish a recognizable, scalable visual standard for Central Church / Water's Edge learning while giving each approved course the treatment its audience and purpose require. Courses will look polished, feel intuitive, function reliably, and preserve the course writer's intended content and flow. Video and audio will meet an agreed professional standard, learner-facing assets will be accessible and optimized for online use, and course builds will pass review and testing before publication. Success will also be evident in disciplined collaboration: authorized projects move forward on schedule; content questions are returned to the appropriate owner; project status and hours remain visible; and templates, assets, and source files are organized so courses can be maintained, refreshed, and expanded over time. organization.name: Scaling.com
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: About Scaling.com Scaling.com helps established business owners 10x their companies in three years or less. As far as we know, we are the only true scaling research advisory firm in the world. Not “growth,” but scale. We work with entrepreneurs doing $1 million or more in revenue (With many of our clients between $100M and $1B+) who are ready to stop being the bottleneck and build a company that scales. Our creative library includes multiple NYT best-selling books, large podcast appearances, keynotes, live events, client/member interviews, case studies, client/member training material, webinars, founder content, and hundreds of verified customer stories. Why This Role Exists Scaling.com tests hundreds of hooks each week. When the market tells us a hook is working, this role turns that signal into a larger family of direct-response video ads. We are looking for someone who has already written high-performing video creative and scripts at the volume and quality required to support multiple millions of dollars in monthly ad spend. You will not begin with a blank page. You will receive a winning hook, a proven video ad, or a clear performance signal. Your job is to understand why it worked, find the strongest evidence and source material connected to it in our media library, develop the angle, write new versions, and hand the production team a clear creative direction that can become a finished ad. This is primarily a video-ad strategy and scriptwriting role. It combines direct-response strategy, AI-assisted research, source mining, writing, creative iteration, and performance learning. You should also be capable of handling other direct-response copywriting needs when required, but video scripts are the center of the job. Requirements Your Core Workflow Receive winning hooks, proven video ads, winners and losers, hook data, creative references, and testing requests from our Head of Content and paid-media team. Diagnose why it worked: the audience, pain, belief, promise, proof, curiosity, identity, or objection it activated. Continually contribute original concepts, competitor references, and new test ideas to the team's shared concept pool. Use AI to search our content database for supporting material across testimonials, founder podcasts, books, posts, keynotes, trainings, member stories, and excerpts from our twice-yearly live events. Stay deeply current by regularly consuming our books, every founder podcast appearance and keynote, live-event content, trainings, and the weekly case-study podcast produced for our members. Build an evidence bank around the angle. This may include dozens of testimonials, short proof points, founder clips, book lines, customer language, objections, and supporting stories. Write three or four new hook options, develop the body, choose the proof sequence, and create a clear flow for the video ad. Package the developed angle for a Creative Producer and Editor. Give them the message, key lines, source material, intended flow, and what the ad must accomplish without prescribing every visual decision. Review the finished ad to protect the strategy and clarify anything that was lost in execution. When an ad wins, create new variations by changing the hook, body, proof, order, framing, or CTA, and by recombining elements from multiple winners. When the paid-media team flags a winning ad for refresh, identify what should be preserved and what should change so the next version can beat it. Repeat the cycle quickly. Some ads may only perform for a few weeks because we intend to scale spend aggressively. What You Own Winning-hook expansion Angle development AI-assisted source research Testimonial and proof mining Video ad scripts and copy Hook and body variations Creative briefs and source packages Winner iteration Winner refreshes Performance learning Claim and source accuracy What Success Looks Like A dependable flow of strong, evidence-backed angles keeps the production team moving. New video ads come from proven market signals without becoming minor copies of the original. Winning video ads produce useful creative families as the paid-media team scales them. Research is fast, deep, traceable, and materially improves the writing. Editors and designers receive enough direction to protect the message while still owning the execution. The work produces qualified demand, not merely clicks or internal enthusiasm. What We Need to See Direct-response video-ad work with clear personal ownership and measurable outcomes such as spend, qualified leads, booked calls, conversion, revenue, or lift against a control. Your past work should demonstrate the volume, quality, and judgment required to sustain multiple millions of dollars in monthly ad spend. The ability to explain why a hook or ad worked and how you turned that learning into the next test. Experience selling a complex, intangible, high-consideration offer. Expert-led, education, or information businesses are strongly preferred. Strong research judgment across transcripts, testimonials, long-form content, books, customer language, and performance data. A real AI-enabled research and writing workflow that increased speed or creative range without producing generic work. Fast, decisive collaboration with producers, editors, and designers. Excellent judgment around claims, testimonials, attribution, and source accuracy. This Role Is Not Brand copy without a measurable action Generic content strategy Starting every assignment from a blank page Prompt output passed off as thinking A writer who disappears after handoff A project-management layer between strategy and production How to Apply Send one direct-response video ad or campaign you personally shaped. Explain the original signal or insight, the audience, the hook, the angle, the proof, the measurable result, and what you created next. Include the numbers and your exact ownership. Then show us how you use AI to search, organize, and turn a large body of source material into a stronger ad. We want to see the workflow and the finished result, not a list of tools. Benefits PTO US Holidays Originally posted on Himalayas

input.description: About Kobo Kobo is a nonprofit technology organization that creates and supports open-source tools and services to improve how data is collected, managed, and used in humanitarian, development, and human rights work. We equip communities and organizations with the technology, training, insights, and services they need to turn field data into real-world change. Our primary platform, KoboToolbox , is used by over 35,000 nonprofit organizations worldwide to collect more than 25 million surveys per month, driving impactful, data-driven decisions to solve the world’s most complex problems. Role Summary The Multimedia Graphic Designer will play a critical role in advancing Kobo’s external communication and fundraising goals by creating compelling visual content that tells powerful stories, engages new and existing donors, and builds brand awareness. This position combines traditional graphic design with video production, photography, animation, and audio to produce engaging digital content for all of Kobo’s web, social media, and online learning channels. In this newly created position, the Multimedia Graphic Designer will bridge art and technology. In this role, they will also identify and coordinate with external video and photography providers as needed, for example, for the creation of impactful donor-focused videos to showcase Kobo’s impact in supporting humanitarian organizations on the ground. The ideal candidate is a creative storyteller with a passion for mission-driven work, skilled at translating complex impact data and beneficiary stories into visually engaging assets that inspire giving. They are an expert in brand storytelling and stewardship. Key Responsibilities Graphic Design & Branding Design and produce a wide range of fundraising and communications materials, including donor communications, social media imagery, brochures, impact infographics, digital banners, digital content for two websites, and dynamic presentation decks via PowerPoint or a similar tool. Maintain and evolve organizational brand standards (including presentation templates and corporate stationery) to ensure consistency across all visual communications, while adapting designs for different donor audiences (e.g., high-net-worth individuals, foundations, corporate partners, or potential customers). Create campaign-specific visuals that support major gift cultivation, individual giving programs, and online donor engagement. Develop and manage a digital asset library (photos, videos, animation, graphics, templates) for efficient reuse across teams. Manage the organization's brand architecture and create and maintain brand guidelines; collaborate with teams and stakeholders to build cohesive visuals aligned with the organization's goals. Assist with donor-facing digital tools, such as campaign landing pages, e-newsletters, and virtual event materials. Support a mobile-first website strategy with dynamic visual content and ensure accessibility standards. Videography and Photography Plan and produce professional videography and photography material for field programs, storytelling, and impact documentation. This includes personally capturing content as well as recruiting and supervising external partners on the ground. Edit and finalize all photo and video assets. Produce compelling images and footage that authentically represent the organization’s work, with sensitivity to cultural contexts and privacy considerations (especially in humanitarian or global health contexts). Edit and optimize photo/video content for various uses: websites, social media (such as Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn), grant proposals, and stewardship materials. Edit and assemble raw footage, incorporating sound effects and adding visual special effects. Create engaging social media visuals, short-form videos, and motion graphics to drive donor acquisition, storytelling, and awareness campaigns. Requirements Need to Have: Proficiency in tools such as Figma (a primary tool we utilize), Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere Pro, After Effects, Lightroom), or other relevant tools (e.g., Affinity, Canva, CapCut). Passion for Mission: Demonstrated commitment to the organization’s cause (e.g., humanitarian aid, global health, or development work). Experience utilizing AI tools responsibly to quickly scale variations of ad creatives and assets. Strong Creative Thinking You should be able to understand a product and its customer, then turn that information into clear and varied ad concepts. input.description: About Builders Builders is a non-partisan movement of millions, uniting Americans across lines of difference - grounded in the belief that curiosity, compassion, courage, and creativity can move us beyond division. Founded by Daniel Lubetzky, our community spans 5M+ citizens, 650M video views, and 400+ movement partners including José Andrés, Katie Couric, Adam Grant, Lonnie Ali, and Karl Rove. Through a growing ecosystem of content, tools, partnerships, and activations, we turn civic engagement into meaningful action - empowering people to participate, collaborate, and deliver real-world impact to enact lasting change. About the Position The media landscape has fundamentally changed - and Builders needs someone who not only knows that, but is already living it. We’re looking for a communications professional who has mastered the brass tacks of traditional PR - the pitch, the placement, the press release, the relationships - and who also sees clearly where media is heading and knows how to operate there. Reporting to the Editorial Director and CMO, you will be the engine behind Builders’ day-to-day earned media operation - driving coverage across traditional outlets, independent media, and creator platforms alike. You think in audiences, not just outlets. You use technology to move faster and smarter. And you bring a point of view on where the media ecosystem is going - not just where it has been. This is an ideal role for a PR professional who has done the foundational work and is ready to help define what modern communications looks like for one of the most important civic movements in the country. Responsibilities Earned Media & Pitching Own the daily pitch operation - proactively identifying story angles, drafting sharp pitches, and relentlessly following up to secure coverage across national media outlets and key regional markets (most notably, Texas). Monitor the news and culture cycle in real time to spot reactive opportunities where Builders’ voice, insights, or programs can be inserted credibly and quickly. Draft compelling press releases, media advisories, op-ed drafts, and story memos that make it easy for journalists to say yes. Develop and maintain a robust media list across national political, civic, and cultural beats. Treat creators as a core earned media channel - identifying, vetting, and building relationships with podcasters, newsletter writers, YouTube channels, and social creators whose audiences align with Builders’ mission and reach demographics traditional press doesn’t. Managing execution in collaboration with the Social team. Media Relationships Build and maintain genuine, trust-based relationships with journalists, producers, editors, and bookers across print, digital, broadcast, and podcast platforms. Serve as a consistent, reliable point of contact for media - responding quickly, providing useful background, and positioning Builders as a go-to source for cross-partisan civic stories. Identify and cultivate relationships with emerging media voices and non-traditional platforms where Builders’ message can reach new audiences. Support the placement and preparation of Builders spokespeople and Movement Partners for media appearances, interviews, and contributed content opportunities. Technology & Tools Leverage AI tools actively across your workflow - pitch drafting, media research, coverage analysis, and contact list building - staying ahead of emerging PR tech.
