input.title: Sr. Product Marketing Manager

organization.name: Thanx
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: Who Are We? Thanx is a leading loyalty and guest engagement platform for regional and national restaurants. We help brands drive profitable growth by increasing guest frequency, growing digital sales, and reducing reliance on discounts. Most loyalty platforms work for guests who are already loyal. Thanx unifies loyalty, digital ordering, and marketing automation in one platform that turns first-time and casual guests into regulars, treating loyalty as a business outcome, not a program, and engaging across the entire guest base. Thanx has raised more than $30M from elite investors including M33 Growth, Ribbit Capital, and Sequoia Capital. Our success is rooted in a culture that has attracted some of the best talent in the country, and we are proud of strong employee tenure, a track record of internal promotions, and the company-wide shift to working AI-native over the last 18 months. We credit our cultural “core behaviors” with these accomplishments: Think Boldly, Execute Reliably, Focus on What Matters, Say “ Thanx ” Genuinely, Encourage Diverse Perspectives, and Lead, Virtually. Who Are You? You're a product marketer who owns outcomes, not output. You are naturally curious about customers and not-yet customers. You write well and fast, and you get real satisfaction out of turning a customer's results into something a salesperson, a CSM, or a prospect can immediately use. You've spent enough time in growth-stage B2B SaaS to know how companies like ours work: how sales cycles move, what CS teams need, why launches succeed or stall. You have run launches where you set the strategy, not just the deliverables, and you have built positioning that sales adopted because it worked, not because you told them to. You decide what matters and what doesn't. You hold a steady output of high-quality material, you figure things out when the path isn't obvious, and you notice a gap and fill it before anyone assigns it. You are equally comfortable briefing the exec team and sitting on a customer call taking notes. Everyone at Thanx has equity and is expected to operate like an owner. That means real intensity, including evenings and weekends when the work calls for it. If that isn't what you're looking for right now, this isn't the right role. We would rather you know that before you apply than after you start. Position Overview Thanx ships a lot. That effort only matters if the market, our prospects, and our own customers understand it and adopt it. The range is wide: big agentic AI launches like our most recent, RecoveryAI; technical ones like Square ordering, where the value exists in the minutia; and everything in between. Each has a different goal, and you work backward from that goal rather than running the same playbook every time. That's this role. You own how the market understands what we build. You set launch strategy, own positioning and messaging for the surface areas you cover, and turn what our customers are doing into proof that makes the value obvious to prospects, customers, internal teams, and partners. You report to the VP of Marketing and operate as a peer to sales, CS, product, and partnerships leadership. You will lead cross-functional launch teams without formal authority over them, brief the exec team on what is and isn't landing in market, and make the call on what we do and don't invest in. How We Work With AI What Thanx gives you AI capability at Thanx is infrastructure, not a perk. You will be given the tools, the budget, and the working culture to get good at this quickly: Real token budgets. You will not be rationed on the tool you use to do your work. Keystone. Our homegrown connective tissue that puts company data and tooling into a queryable, natural-language format. The Grid. An internal site to host AI-built applications, reports, and tools that can be shared company-wide. A show-and-tell culture. People here demo what they have built, and it becomes something the rest of the company uses. Getting up the learning curve is a shared project, not a solo one. A growing library of tools we built ourselves. Marketing runs its own marketing calendar app, marketing dashboard, competitive intelligence hub, case study asset builder, and sales demo platform. You will add to it: build the tools that take repeatable work off your plate, and hold the output to a higher standard. What we expect from you You treat AI as a working partner. You know the output is only as good as the context you give it and the review you do afterward, and you invest time in both. You build or improve things other people use . When you solve a problem, you put in the extra effort to make the solution reusable, so nobody on your team has to solve it again. Then you do the harder part: make it good enough, and obvious enough, that using it beats going back to the old way. You do not wait to be assigned the work. You notice when a one-off request is really a recurring problem, and you decide it is worth solving before anyone asks you to. At review time, the question is not how much you used AI. It is what you built, who else is using it, and how your team works differently because of it. What it looks like in this role You build the tool that makes the content. Instead of just writing the case study, you also build what orchestrates the whole case study production process: one customer interview in, a dozen usable formats out, page drafts in Webflow, deck content, and social assets that don't wait on a designer. Sales and CS run it themselves rather than queuing behind you, and the test is whether what comes out is usable without review cycles. You find the stories in the product. You use our internal analytical AI tool, Sherlock, to investigate how customers actually run their business on Thanx , surfacing the learnings and outcomes that today only exist in our CSMs' heads. You turn those golden nuggets into externally facing content in days, not weeks. Gone are the days of long-form content that takes months to produce. You get content seen. You treat distribution as half the job. You keep trying formats until one breaks through: video, podcasts, live events, office hours, community forums, whatever gets the audience to show up, and you use AI to make the learning curve shorter and the output more fun. You know the market and the competitive landscape cold. You use AI to listen for and understand what competitors are shipping and what operators are actually dealing with - traffic softness, labor costs, delivery margins - and can explain how those connect to what we sell and how we are different. Key Responsibilities Positioning and messaging. Own product-level positioning and messaging for the platform areas you cover. Build the frameworks, get sales and CS to adopt them, and revise them as the market and the roadmap change. You are the person who decides how we talk about what we build, and the person who defends that choice when someone disagrees. Launch strategy and delivery. Own launches end to end: set the tier, define the goal, choose the tactics that fit that goal, run the cross-functional team, and report honestly on what worked. You decide what gets a full launch and what gets a release note, and you make that call based on business impact, not internal enthusiasm. Customer stories and proof. Own the proof library, not just the individual stories. Interview newly launched customers and the internal teams behind them, find the unique angle, and produce everything from short reference stories to full case studies with quotes, metrics, and narrative. Build the system that turns one interview into one-pagers, slides, use case documentation, and the proof that answers "show me someone doing this" and "when would I use this feature?" Know where the gaps in our proof are before sales tells you. Enablement for sales, CS, and partners. Own what those teams know and say about the platform. Build the training, the competitive positioning, and the objection handling, then measure whether it is being used and whether win rates moved. Work directly with sales and CS leadership on where the gaps are. Market and competitive command. Own our point of view on what competitors are shipping and what restaurant operators are actually dealing with. Bring that back into positioning, roadmap conversations, and exec discussions. Be the person the exec team asks when they want to know what is happening in market. External and in-product content. Keep a regular cadence of customer-win content for social and partner channels ("this brand launched this week, here's why it's interesting"), and apply a product marketing lens to the Help Center and in-dashboard content: embedded video, plus the context that explains why and when to use a feature, not just how it works. How We Will Know It's Working At six months: you have run at least one Tier-1 launch end to end, sales is using messaging you wrote, and you have published proof for customers who launched on your watch. At twelve months: positioning is largely owned by you, the exec team comes to you for market intel, and the systems you have built mean the next launch takes less of everyone's time than the last one. What We’re Looking For We don't believe in rigid requirements, but success in this role typically involves: 8+ years in B2B SaaS, including 5-7 years in product marketing, customer marketing, or a closely adjacent role. Ownership of at least one major product launch end to end, including the strategy and the tradeoffs, not just the deliverables. Positioning or messaging work that sales and CS actually adopted, and a clear account of how you got them to. A portfolio of written work you can walk us through, including case studies, product content, and enablement materials, and a clear sense of what it accomplished. Experience conducting customer interviews and finding the story inside them. Strong instincts for learning core personas, and for adapting the same material across prospects, customers, internal teams, and partners. A track record of working productively with sales and customer success, and of creating enablement content those teams actually used. Experience influencing cross-functional teams you don't manage, and presenting to executives. Comfort with video and multimedia formats, not just written content. Restaurant or hospitality technology experience is a plus. Compensation: US - Tier 1 $165,000 - $182,000 USD US - Tier 2 $154,000 - $168,000 USD US - Tier 3 $146,000 - $160,000 USD Canada $138,000 - $148,000 CAD Leveling & Location: Thanx uses structured internal leveling and location-based compensation. Final leveling and compensation are determined through the interview process based on experience, scope, and work location, and any offer will align with the appropriate range. Application Process: This position is an existing vacancy. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in screening or assessing applications; human review will always remain part of the process. Ready to change your life? Apply now! We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity company. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. Thanx will consider qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records for employment in a manner consistent with local requirements. Originally posted on Himalayas

input.description: This is a remote position. Turn briefs and raw footage into scroll-stopping, high-volume video ads that drive conversion for a mission-driven e-commerce brand. Location: Remote Role Type: Contract | Consultant-contractor | Ongoing monthly (volume-based) Reports to: Creative Director / Creative Strategist The opportunity Our client is scaling its creative output for Meta from roughly 12 to 30 new concepts per month. They are seeking a Video Editor to take written briefs and folders of footage and reliably produce finished, high-quality video at pace. In this role, you will cut ads built specifically for Meta placements (feed, reels, stories), collaborate with the Creative Strategist and Creative Director to maintain brand standards, and help ensure the account never runs dry by delivering fast, clean revisions across a high-velocity pipeline. About the organization Our client is a mission-driven e-commerce brand focused on olive oil and related products, committed to authentic storytelling without fake urgency or hard-sell gimmicks. The creative team is currently focused on rebuilding their editing bench to raise both craft and speed, ensuring that every asset—from cold outreach to retargeting—maintains a "hook-first" approach while keeping the customer as the hero. What you will do Cut finished video ads to brief, ensuring a strong hook in the first second, tight pacing, captions, and sound design ready for immediate deployment on Meta. Quality and retention-focused editing is the #1 priority. Resize and reframe single concepts into multiple assets for different funnel stages (cold, consideration, retargeting) and placements (feed, reels, stories). Maintain high volume and speed, managing reliable turnaround times and handling revision rounds efficiently within a fast-paced workflow. Apply motion graphics, subtitles, color correction, and simple animation to meet the client’s specific brand and quality standards. Produce a range of video content beyond paid ads, including organic social cuts, website/PDP videos, email clips, UGC edits, and localized/subtitled versions. What you bring Demonstrated ability to edit short-form DTC ads for paid social, shown through a reel featuring performed Meta ads rather than just montages or film-festival style work. Fluent proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects (or DaVinci Resolve), with strong skills in captioning, motion graphics, and sound design. Experience working at volume, demonstrating calm reliability and speed under a consistent, high-cadence production schedule. Must be comfortable handling ~30 concepts/month across multiple placements. Low-ego, brief-driven mindset with the ability to take direction clearly and iterate quickly based on feedback. Understanding of Meta-specific metrics such as hook rate and retention, prioritizing commercial effectiveness over artistic abstraction. Helpful, but not essential Mission fluency, particularly if you are Palestinian or have a genuine connection to the brand’s story and values. Ability to shoot video in addition to editing, allowing for greater versatility in content creation. Experience in other e-commerce verticals or direct-to-consumer brands with similar scaling needs. How the engagement works Contracting party: You will contract directly with Apricot, which will manage contracting, invoicing/payroll, payments, and administrative support. Day to day, you will work with the client’s creative team and report to the Creative Director/Creative Strategist. For this consultant engagement, your work will be based on ongoing monthly delivery. The role begins with a paid trial consisting of one or two cuts from real briefs to assess fit, followed by a continuing monthly contract. You are expected to provide your own laptop and basic equipment, maintain reliable connectivity, and follow required security controls. Planned check-ins are scheduled for month 1 and month 3 to see how the engagement is working and help address any issues. About Apricot Apricot is a nonprofit sourcing firm connecting displaced and underserved professionals from Palestine and the wider MENA region with global employment opportunities. We combine a clear social-impact mission with fast, high-quality recruitment delivery for international clients. Originally posted on Himalayas

input.description: We are a startup building AI agents and consumer devices. Users prompt agents to take actions across their tools, and use our custom devices to capture intent on the go. We are a small team based in Shenzhen and New York and our founder previously started a unicorn company in Silicon Valley. We are looking for a few freelance CG artists to help create high-quality product images and videos for our smart ring. You will work from product references, CAD/STP files, CMF direction, and factory samples to produce polished renders, short videos, turntables, and motion assets for website, ads, social, investor materials, and product decision-making. This is a freelance role. We care most about taste, speed, realism, motion sense, and the ability to turn loose direction into strong visual output without heavy hand-holding. Responsibilities Create photorealistic renders of a small consumer hardware product, primarily a smart ring. Produce product images and videos for website, ads, social, pitch decks, and internal design reviews. Create short product videos, turntables, motion tests, launch visuals, and social/ad clips. Animate camera moves, product reveals, material transitions, LED states, charging moments, and simple interaction concepts. Build realistic material studies across ceramic, metal, resin, glass, plastic, LED, and charging/contact details. Create multiple CMF and finish explorations quickly from loose references. Work with CAD/STP files, product photos, factory drawings, and reference images. Set up clean lighting, camera angles, surfaces, and compositions that make a small wearable product feel premium. Deliver organized source files and export-ready still/video assets in clean, reusable formats. Iterate quickly based on feedback from product, marketing, and hardware teams. Requirements Strong portfolio of product rendering work, ideally consumer electronics, wearables, jewelry, watches, rings, or small hardware. Strong portfolio of product video, animation, motion graphics, or short 3D product ads. Excellent sense of lighting, materials, composition, scale, and product detail. Experience with Blender, Cinema 4D, KeyShot, Redshift, Octane, V-Ray, After Effects, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, or similar rendering/video tools. Comfortable working from imperfect inputs: CAD files, rough product references, factory samples, and written direction. Able to move quickly and produce polished outputs without a large creative team around you. Strong file organization and ability to deliver final images, final videos, and editable project files. Good written communication and responsiveness. Helpful but not required Experience rendering jewelry, ceramic, titanium, PVD finishes, transparent/translucent materials, or compact electronics. Ability to combine 3D renders with AI video/image tools where useful. Familiarity with DFM, CMF, industrial design, or factory communication. Experience using AI image/video tools as part of a rendering or concept workflow. Ability to lightly retouch or composite final outputs in Photoshop. What we care about Can you make a tiny object look expensive, real, desirable, and dynamic? Can you create several visual directions fast, not just one perfect render slowly? Can you create motion that explains the product without making it feel like a generic tech ad? Can you understand product constraints without needing every detail specified? Can your work help us make product and marketing decisions, not just look nice? Application questions Portfolio: link to your best product rendering and product video work. Tools: what software/render engines/video tools do you use? Hardware experience: have you rendered jewelry, wearables, consumer electronics, or small physical products before? Workflow: if we give you a STEP file, product references, and CMF notes, what is your usual process from intake to final stills and video? Motion: what types of product videos can you make well: turntables, short ads, product reveals, material studies, UI/device interaction, or something else? Speed: how quickly can you usually turn around a first pass for 3-5 product render or video directions? Availability: how many freelance hours per week can you take on? input.description: Founded in 1981 in partnership with whistleblowers, the Project On Government Oversight (POGO) is a nonpartisan independent watchdog that works to expose waste, corruption, abuse of power, and other instances where the government fails to serve the public. We champion reforms to achieve a more effective, ethical, and accountable federal government that safeguards constitutional principles. POGO has an over $7 million annual budget that supports a staff of over 50 employees. POGO is looking for a talented Social Media Editor to be our newsroom's day to day social media lead. This role owns the execution of the POGO Investigates social strategy across X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Instagram and Facebook, turning investigations into native, platform-first content that delivers findings directly to readers and grows POGO Investigates as a credible presence in accountability journalism. This position reports to the Digital Engagement Manager. We encourage potential applicants to apply even if they only have experience or familiarity in some of the areas described below. We fully recognize that many great candidates will not have experience in all of the areas we list, or may have relevant experiences and skills that we have not listed or considered. Responsibilities include: Owns the POGO Investigates social content calendar and produces the native package for every investigation launch: X and Bluesky threads and in-post summaries, LinkedIn long-form posts and native document posts, Instagram carousels, Reels, Stories, and data cards, and Facebook visual summaries. Writes social copy in the POGO Investigates voice (confident, intellectual, conversational, nonpartisan, independent; grounded in evidence rather than advocacy) that puts the findings ahead of the links and holds to the strategy's content mix targets (roughly 70 percent native, 30 percent link). Produces recurring content across the newsroom's content pillars, including standalone data points, archive features, behind-the-investigation and reporter spotlight content, and impact and outcomes posts, so the accounts stay active between investigation drops. Creates and edits short-form video (30 to 60 seconds), pull-quote and data graphics, and document snapshots using established templates and the Brand Kit; works with the associate designer and Creative team on higher-production assets. Builds and maintains an evergreen content bank by auditing raw and published assets (interview footage, B-roll, testimony clips, data visualizations, podcast audio, published data) and clipping them into platform-ready formats. Drives email list growth in coordination with the Digital Engagement Manager through social, including link stickers, newsletter conversion pushes, and automation tools such as ManyChat where adopted. Tracks performance in Sprout Social and native platform analytics against the PI strategy's benchmarks (follower retention, platform engagement rates, content mix, LinkedIn growth) and reports weekly during launch and monthly thereafter. Works closely with the Digital team's social media manager and digital engagement staff to align the POGO Investigates accounts with POGO's main channels, including collaborative posts, cross-posting ,share content, and avoid duplication. Qualifications include: Three years of experience running social media for a newsroom, news outlet, or journalism nonprofit, with a track record of packaging reported stories for social platforms. Demonstrated ability to create native content across formats, including written threads, carousels, short-form video, and data graphics, using tools such as Canva, Adobe Express or Creative Cloud, CapCut, or comparable software. Strong news judgment and story instincts: can identify the lead finding in a long investigation, write tight and accurate copy, and work within journalistic standards for sourcing and attribution. Excellent writing and editing skills with the ability to adapt voice by platform while staying consistent with a newsroom brand. Experience with social media management and analytics tools (Sprout Social or similar) and the ability to translate performance data into content decisions. Ability to work under deadline, manage a multi-platform calendar, and coordinate across reporters, newsroom leadership, editors, designers, and communications staff. Understanding of nonpartisan communications and the judgment to cover politically charged subjects without partisan framing. Commitment to POGO's mission and values, including equity and inclusion. (+) Experience at an investigative or accountability-focused outlet, or covering federal government, Congress, or public policy. (+) Basic video editing and motion graphics skills, and experience directing or shooting reporter-facing video. (+) Experience building or relaunching a social presence, including audience retention through a rebrand or acquisition. (+) Familiarity with LinkedIn newsletters, native document posts, and audience development among policy and professional audiences. Compensation, benefits, and other information: This position is eligible for remote work from anywhere within the United States provided you are available during POGO's working hours of 9AM-6PM EST. This is a full-time, non-exempt, at will position. This position is grant funded for a period of one year and continued employment is contingent upon the receipt of direct grant funds. This position includes the listed benefits: Competitive nonprofit salary commensurate with experience in the range of $74K - $80K annually Health, dental and vision insurance 403(b) employee investment plan available, with employer contribution once eligible Life insurance, short-term and long-term disability coverage Paid holiday, vacation, and sick leave To Apply: Resume required, cover letter welcomed but not required. input.description: We are on a mission to make everything you see shoppable, starting with what you watch. We believe that Silvr will set the bar for how we experience and engage with content, and we’d love for you to join us on our journey! We’re not looking for an intern to fetch coffee. We’re looking for a Marketing and Social Media Architect —a self-starting, creative, and highly outgoing individual who lives and breathes digital culture and loves building something from nothing. Our company is building the next generation of visual search for fashion. We are solving the universal consumer pain point: instantly finding and locating the exact outfit, item, or accessory seen in TV shows, movies, and social media videos. This is a massive, untapped market, and we need someone who can dive into communities obsessed with fashion across all platforms and scream about it. If you thrive on autonomy, if you see a digital challenge and immediately think of five unconventional ways to solve it, and if you want to be the voice and write the playbook for the best app that hasn't launched yet, this role is for you. What You'll Be Doing: The High-Impact Hustle This is an action-oriented role focused on connecting directly with our future users through high-impact, low-cost (guerrilla) tactics: Demand Generation & The Hunt: Become our dedicated brand ambassador on platforms like Instagram and TikTok . You will be on-camera often, and you will actively seek out individuals struggling with the problem we solve—people asking, "Where is this outfit from?" or "Help me find this coat from that movie." You will engage genuinely, introduce our solution, and create immediate brand advocates. Have an idea for a collaboration? Pitch it. Want to jump on a trend? Go for it. Figure out what works and double down. Culture Curation: Define our brand's conversational voice. You will be pitching and executing marketing initiatives across online communities (Reddit, Discord, niche forums, etc.) and real-world spaces (college campuses). Consumer Intelligence: Conduct primary consumer research through interviews and structured surveys. You will gather critical insights on what features users want, what frustrates them, and how we need to talk about our product. You will present your critical insights directly to the founding team (CEO and CTO). Creative Asset Support: Work closely with our core team to brainstorm and execute artistic and creative content. Launch, Iterate, & Pivot: Every week, you will launch new, outside-the-box marketing ideas and immediately analyze the data. You are expected to be a proactive problem-solver who can spot failed tactics and make real-time adjustments to drive results. Success Looks Like: The 90-Day Mission Your success will be measured by your ability to drive engaged, high-quality user growth based on the following metrics: Active User Acquisition: Driving a significant volume of app downloads where users are highly engaged and make at least one purchase. Generating high-quality users who see immediate value is the ultimate goal. Platform Engagement & Traffic: Measurable growth in key platform metrics (e.g., TikTok followers/comments , Instagram shares/saves/engagement ) that correlate directly to website traffic (monitored via Google Analytics ) and app downloads. Iterative Results: Demonstrating the ability to execute, analyze failures, and rapidly pivot your strategy to improve performance week over week. Why Join Silvr ? We’re big on transparency; when we make decisions, you’ll always know why. Our founders are deeply involved in the day-to-day and maintain an open-door policy to ensure everyone feels connected to the vision. If you have a question about our progress, a solution to a problem, or a picture of your pet that needs to be shown off, you can always find us. We love our work, and we also understand that life doesn’t fit neatly into a 9-to-5 schedule. That’s why we’re fully remote and flexible to meet the needs of our team. Whether it’s family, appointments, or personal commitments, we trust our people to manage their time in a way that works for them. At Silvr , you’ll be part of a close-knit team that values fun, flexibility, freedom, and a commitment to world changing innovation. Who You Are: Your DNA Extroverted and Outgoing: You love talking to people, both online and off. You are comfortable approaching strangers (virtually or physically) and engaging them in meaningful conversations about our product and the problem we solve. A True Self-Starter: You require minimal oversight. When given a goal, you figure out the path and execute it, learning quickly and adapting along the way. You follow workflow guidelines and turn in work on time to meet deadlines. Detail-Oriented: This is critical for consumer research. Your messages are clear, engaging, persuasive, and always professional, regardless of the platform. You can help draft an email to pitch an influencer, and follow-up in a timely fashion with leads. input.description: About Pavilion Pavilion began as a bold experiment to solve a personal problem. Those peer conversations – equal parts therapy, strategy, and camaraderie – sparked a global community of GTM professionals united by shared learning and support. Today, Pavilion serves nearly 10,000 members worldwide with industry-leading retention and profitability. At over $10M ARR, the brand is synonymous with excellence in GTM leadership. The Opportunity We're seeking a Vice President of Marketing to lead Pavilion 's next era of growth—defining how we attract, engage, and retain members across their full journey. This is a high-impact leadership role for a strategist with expertise in today’s growth marketing tactics, who blends creativity with discipline and understands that long-term growth depends on both attraction and retention. Demand generation expertise is central to this role: you should be someone who has personally built and run acquisition programs, not just directed them through partners. You should also be fluent in building AI-driven tools and workflows — able to speak concretely about agents or automations you've built and the measurable impact they had on a marketing team's output. Core Responsibilities Growth Oversight (≈30%) Bring demand generation expertise directly to the table: paid, SEO, and event acquisition programs, whether run in-house or supported by agencies. Manage external agencies running paid, SEO, and event campaigns, with the credibility to evaluate and challenge their strategy rather than simply relay it. Maintain ROI discipline and brand alignment across acquisition programs. Test and evaluate new channels to reach GTM professionals globally. AI-Driven Enablement Build and deploy AI agents and automated workflows that support marketing functions — for example, content production, segmentation, campaign reporting, and/or lead scoring. Bring specific, namable examples of AI tools or agents you've built in past roles, along with the business impact they had (time saved, output increased, cost reduced, etc.). Stay ahead of emerging AI technologies and embed them into team workflows. Member Lifecycle Marketing Create programs that drive activation, engagement, and renewal. Partner with Sales & Success on onboarding, nurture, and milestone communications. Develop referral and win-back campaigns that turn satisfied members into advocates. Brand & Communications Lead Pavilion 's brand presence across web, social, events, and content. Oversee thought leadership, PR, and storytelling that elevate Pavilion 's reputation and member value. Collaborate with Education and Community teams to highlight member success and insights. Strategy & Leadership Build an integrated marketing plan that balances brand storytelling, lifecycle engagement, and scalable growth. Translate Pavilion 's mission into clear messaging across every touchpoint—from awareness through renewal. Partner with leadership to evolve brand architecture and positioning. Define and measure success across acquisition, retention, and member satisfaction. Lead a small, high-performing team (3–4 people). Foster collaboration, accountability, and creative excellence. Establish key marketing KPIs, dashboards, and optimization frameworks. Required Skills & Experience 8+ years in marketing, including 3–5 in leadership within membership, community, or subscription models. Demonstrated demand generation expertise — direct, hands-on experience building and running paid, SEO, or other acquisition programs, not solely managing agencies. Proven success in integrated brand and lifecycle marketing. Experience managing agencies or contractors for acquisition programs. Hands-on experience building AI agents or AI-driven workflows for marketing use cases, with the ability to name specific tools or systems built and describe their measurable impact. Strong content and communications background; comfort with analytics and budgets. Excellent collaboration and communication skills. Preferred: Experience in B2B SaaS or professional development; understanding of retention tactics, event marketing, and community storytelling. What Success Looks Like First 90 Days Audit demand generation and lifecycle performance. Identify quick wins for engagement and retention. Recommend and begin building AI tools/agents and process improvements. Build alignment with leadership and member-facing teams. First Year Improved engagement, retention, and referral metrics. Efficient, brand-aligned acquisition, with demonstrated hands-on demand gen contribution. Clear ROI from AI agents and workflows built and deployed within the team. Unified brand and communication framework. Marketing positioned as a driver of both growth and member satisfaction. Why Pavilion ? Be part of a mission-driven organization that prioritizes the professional growth and success of its members above all. input.title: Director, Content

organization.name: Darkroom
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: About the Role We're looking for a senior content leader to own the voice of two brands: Darkroom , our growth marketing agency, and Shadow , our AI commerce platform. Ad Age recently described us as "if Omnicom was rebuilt on AI." Your job is to turn a line like that into an argument the market repeats back to us. The split is roughly 80% Darkroom , 20% Shadow. We are making a category bet on the forward-deployed marketer , the operator who sits inside a business and builds with AI rather than briefing the work out. We intend to make that a term of art through Darkroom : the article, the LinkedIn engine, the video, the webinars, the press. You own that campaign end to end. You'll report to our VP of Marketing, who sets direction and makes the calls. You'll help shape the thinking behind it: how content maps to the funnel, which channels carry which offers, and what actually turns attention into pipeline. Then you build the content that proves it. Our marketing operations manager owns the calendar, the publishing, and the deployment. You make the content that fills all of it, across LinkedIn, video, email, paid, and creator, and you brief our designer, video editor, and SEO specialist so one idea becomes a post, a video, an email, and an ad in the same week. This isn't a writing-only role. Alongside content, you own the creative half of the creator program: who we work with, what we ask them to make, and the call on whether we go wide with many creators or deep with a few. You source and negotiate the partnerships and write the briefs. Marketing Ops runs the admin behind it. Creator content is one of our two strongest lead sources today and the one with the most room left in it. This is a New York-based role operating in the EST Time Zone, hybrid out of our new NYC office, and all business is conducted 100% in English. What you'll do Brand Narrative: Define and defend what Darkroom and Shadow say. Own the positioning arguments, the category bet, and the point of view that shows up everywhere else. Funnel & Strategy: Work with the VP of Marketing on how content builds pipeline: which channels, which offers, which lead magnets, and what the content has to do at each stage. You help build the model, then you feed it. LinkedIn & Video: Build our LinkedIn engine across the company page and our executives' accounts, including video made for the feed it runs in. This is where our buyers spend their day and where we have the most ground to take. Creator Strategy & Briefs: Decide who we work with and what they make. Source creators, negotiate the partnerships, write the briefs, and set the strategy between a wide roster and a small group of anchor creators. Marketing Ops handles the CRM, deadlines, content collection and reporting. Email & Newsletter: Own what goes into our newsletter and to our list. Marketing Ops handles deployment. The thinking, the cadence, and the reason anyone opens it are yours. Shadow Content: Take Shadow's content from scattered to a funnel: posts into webinars and lead magnets into signups. Product marketing for a platform that sells to operators. Paid Copy: Partner with our designer, video editor and performance team on the words behind our ads, so the organic and creator assets that work become the ads that work. Editorial Direction: Brief the team, review the work, and hold a consistent standard across every surface both brands touch. Events & Moments: Turn our NYC office, our activations, and our press into content programs instead of one-off posts. Measurement: Work with Marketing Ops on the weekly scoreboard: reach, follower growth, earned media value, and how content traffic converts. You should apply if this sounds like you 5+ years in content, brand, or creator marketing, from an agency or a commerce brand, with B2B or pipeline accountability. SaaS or martech experience is a plus. You have owned content that was accountable to a business number. You can explain how a post becomes traffic, becomes a conversion, becomes a lead, and you have been graded at the end of that chain. If content has always been someone else's funnel, this role is not for you. You know this world. DTC, e-commerce, performance marketing, social commerce, AI tooling. You can write about TikTok Shop, retention, or attribution without a briefing and without getting it wrong. You have sourced, negotiated with, and briefed creators yourself. You know what separates a brief that produces something usable from one that wastes everybody's month. You have a public track record. A newsletter, bylines, a brand account you grew, a campaign that landed, a term you helped popularize. Send the link. You get output out of people who don't report to you, and you can give a designer or an editor feedback that makes the next version better. You arrive with a list. In the first interview, we will ask what you would change about our LinkedIn, our newsletter, and our creator content. We expect specifics. You already work with Claude, ChatGPT, or similar daily and have shipped real work with them. We are a Claude-first company. Hard disqualifiers No published writing or no portfolio link. Never sourced or briefed a creator yourself. Content experience with no accountability for pipeline. Equal Opportunity Statement Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace—we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national orientation, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. Originally posted on Himalayas

input.description: Say hello to Hagerty Hagerty is a company built by drivers for drivers. Our Marketplace business presents live and digital sales across the U.S. and Europe, we host a number of driving events and concours, and our award-winning automotive journalists produce the most popular car magazine globally, alongside internationally awarded videos. As an Associate Creative Director, Writer , you’ll help shape how Hagerty shows up as a leader in the automotive space. You’ll develop creative concepts and campaign platforms across brand, marketing, and large-scale initiatives, translating business and audience objectives into compelling ideas and writing. You’ll collaborate closely with Creative Directors, Art Directors, strategists, marketers, and other team members to develop integrated campaigns across channels. You’ll bring a strong creative point of view to the work, take ownership of your assignments, and confidently develop ideas with guidance from creative leadership. As a leader, you’ll also help elevate the work of the team through thoughtful feedback and mentorship while serving as a strong steward of Hagerty ’s brand voice and creative standards. What you’ll do Develop concepts and campaign ideas for integrated brand and marketing campaigns across channels, including large-scale events and key business initiatives. Write compelling, clear, and distinctive headlines, copy, scripts, and other creative content across Hagerty lines of business. Take campaign platform ideas and develop them into strong, channel-specific creative executions. Work with Creative Directors, Art Directors, strategists, producers, marketers, and subject matter experts to develop effective creative solutions. Translate business objectives, audience insights, and brand strategy into compelling creative work. Consider how Hagerty ’s overarching brand story and voice inform each idea and execution. Take ownership of assigned projects from brief through execution, seeking input from creative leadership when needed. Present creative concepts to creative leadership and internal stakeholders, clearly articulating the creative and strategic rationale. Research projects, audiences, industries, cultural trends, and automotive topics to inform creative development. Deliver high-quality work on schedule and communicate proactively when priorities or timelines change. Additional Duties Include Provide thoughtful, actionable feedback and support to copywriters and other creative team members. Help develop and maintain Hagerty ’s brand voice and copywriting guidelines. Make sound copy decisions on assigned projects while incorporating feedback from creative leadership and project partners. Support Creative Directors in presenting and refining work for internal stakeholders. Share relevant industry trends, creative techniques, and emerging technologies with the team. Contribute to a collaborative creative environment with a high bar for the quality of the work. This Might Describe You You love cars, the automotive world and are an enthusiast yourself. You have experience in an advertising agency or strong in-house creative department, concepting, writing, and producing integrated brand and retail campaigns. You’re a strong conceptual thinker who gets excited about developing ideas that can extend across multiple channels. You’re curious about culture, advertising trends, emerging technologies, and new ways to tell stories. You enjoy solving creative problems and finding unexpected ways to make an idea more compelling. You have an exceptional portfolio demonstrating conceptual thinking, writing, and integrated advertising campaigns. Track and compile performance data across platforms, flagging notable trends, changes, concerns, or opportunities for the Senior Social Media Manager. We ensure M+R is positioned to deliver outstanding services to clients such as Planned Parenthood, Feeding America, International Rescue Committee, NRDC, and many more. Day-to-day, our marketing and business development efforts ensure that M+R ’s brand, creative perspective, culture, and expertise are clearly communicated, understood, and consistent across all activities and materials. Here’s what you’ll be doing in this role: The Director, Internal Communications shapes M+R ’s internal messaging by leading employee communication strategies, managing internal channels, and partnering with the People and Culture team to foster a strong company culture. They provide expert counsel on internal and external communications, collaborating with leadership to design and implement strategies that support key M+R initiatives and reinforce business priorities; and play a leadership role in cultivating a workplace environment that aligns with the company’s core values, bridging the work of the People and Culture team, brand identity, and the firm’s communications. Drive the agenda for strategic and/or tactical discussions during bi-weekly Internal Communications Team meetings and monthly all-staff meetings. Support organizational change efforts through thoughtful communication planning, stakeholder engagement, and change management strategies. This includes monitoring Glassdoor and other sites that impact M+R ’s employer brand and presenting recommendations to address concerns raised. Serve as lead strategist and executor of firm-wide teambuilding activities to include all-staff conferences, leadership retreats, and other events. Create and manage content of Homebase, the Broadcast newsletter, bi-weekly marketing digests, town halls, employee surveys, listening sessions, Slack, and other digital or print platforms to optimize employee and stakeholder engagement, and identify themes, trends, and opportunities for improvement. At least 7 years of communications experience preferably in the nonprofit sector or a professional services firm. Exceptional storytelling, grammar, and editing skills with the ability to distill complex information into clear, compelling communications for diverse audiences. Exceptional communicator (oral and written) and active listener with the ability to communicate with candor, clarity, and authenticity; engage thoughtfully with diverse perspectives; and influence and inspire audiences at all levels of the organization. Demonstrated experience in event strategy, planning, and management, including the development and execution of firm-wide events such as all-staff conferences, leadership retreats, town halls, team-building activities, and other employee engagement events; ability to manage event logistics, stakeholder coordination, communications, timelines, and execution from concept through completion. Demonstrated change management experience, including developing and executing communication strategies for organizational change, navigating ambiguity and uncertainty, anticipating stakeholder needs and concerns, and helping to explain the “why”, “what”, and “how” of change. Experience partnering with senior leaders and cross-functional teams to build alignment, address concerns, foster trust and engagement, and support successful adoption of new strategies, structures, processes, programs, or ways of working. Proven experience collaborating across teams and building strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels. Professional and positive approach; self-motivated, collaborative, creative, and able to work independently and take initiative. Demonstrated creative and critical thinking skills with a track record of contributing to culture-building and employee engagement. Strong business acumen, relationship management, strategy development, project management, and problem solving skills. Exercises a high degree of tact, diplomacy, discretion, and sound judgment. Channel Distribution & Performance Optimization: Repurpose core content across channels and collaborate with Digital Marketing to track metrics, test formats, and continuously optimize for audience engagement and lead generation. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Product, Client Marketing, Sales, and Web teams to produce enablement materials, co-marketing collateral, event content, and retention campaigns. Editorial Quality & Workflow Management: Serve as a brand guardian by maintaining top-tier editorial standards across regional variants (US, UK, CA, AU) while seamlessly managing timelines, dependencies, and contributor workflows. What You Bring Demonstrated experience in content marketing, copywriting, editorial, communications, or a related role. Excellent writing, editing, and proofreading skills, with the ability to make complex ideas clear, engaging, and useful. Experience creating content across multiple formats and channels, and coordinating content for integrated campaigns which may include web, email, social media, events, video, or paid digital activity. Strong understanding of how content supports broader marketing objectives, including awareness, engagement, demand generation, client engagement, and conversion. Ability to understand different audiences and adapt messaging, tone, depth, and format accordingly, bringing strong familiarity with US and/or Canadian audiences, culture, and English-language conventions. Experience translating briefs, interviews, research, data, or subject-matter expertise into compelling finished content. Strong editorial judgment, including the ability to identify the strongest angle, distinguish important information from supporting detail, and challenge a brief when a different approach would better achieve the intended outcome. Experience developing and managing organic social media content. Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate, polished, accessible work. Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple content projects and deadlines simultaneously. Ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues across different disciplines and incorporate feedback without losing sight of the purpose and audience of the work. Curiosity and the ability to quickly develop an understanding of unfamiliar topics, audiences, products, and sector issues. Ability to take ownership of an assignment from initial brief through completion, proactively identifying missing information, dependencies, decisions, and next steps. Benefits Company paid medical, dental and vision insurance Generous Paid Time Off benefits, including 21 days of PTO (vacation, personal time, whatever you choose to use it for) 14 paid holidays 10 Paid Sick Days 401(k) with 4% employer match Two paid volunteering days per year Professional development opportunities Flexible working with support for WFH setup / equipment Month-long Paid Sabbatical after 5 years of service Free snacks, drinks and breakfast items in our offices Varied range of regular social activities throughout the year Working From HomeWhile many Spektrix team members live near one of our offices (NYC, London, or Manchester), remote/non-local team members work from home most of the time, and all team members work from home at least some of the time! We provide reasonable support and all the hardware you need to get started, but we do require that you have the have the following in place to work from home: A quiet working space at home where you can consistently take video calls without interruption A strong, reliable internet connection that supports your participation in video calls and access to our systems and service Working At The OfficeFor team members who are 'local' to NYC, a stipend is offered for each day you work on-site. So, however you identify and whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this is a role that would make you excited to come into work every day. Diversity in the workplace is hugely important to our working environment and to enable both individuals and Spektrix to thrive. By valuing each person’s differences we enable each person to contribute their unique experiences, strengths and viewpoints. Workplace diversity is something we aim to achieve and maintain at Spektrix , and we are pursuing a workforce that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve and work in. In an effort to help us reduce bias, please do not include a photo on your resume or application. Originally posted on Himalayas

The American Heart Association (Association) has an excellent opportunity for a Senior Communications Manager - Science Media Relations . This is a position that can be home-based and a flexible location . The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. Be Valued at the American Heart Association by following us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs. Responsibilities In this role, you will be responsible for the implementation of multi-year strategic communication plans supporting and promoting scientific manuscripts published in the American Heart Association ’s 14 peer-reviewed scientific and medical journals, abstracts presented at the Association’s scientific meetings and the Association’s clinical care guidelines, scientific statements and advisories to the media and the public. Responsible for developing appropriate resources and translating the science for the media and the public, to reinforce the Association’s role as a leading voice in cardiovascular and brain health science and care, and the Association’s mission and impact goals. Responsible for securing earned media coverage, establishing and cultivating relationships with journalists, and supporting our science leaders and research authors of scientific manuscripts and abstracts presenting at our scientific meetings or publishing in our scientific journals, and other projects as assigned. Essential Job Duties: Review manuscripts accepted for publication in our scientific journals and abstracts accepted for presentation at our scientific meetings. Develop news releases or other news materials, media pitches, and multi-media assets to promote scientific research featured in abstracts and manuscripts, published in the American Heart Association ’s 14 peer-reviewed scientific journals and/or presented at any of the Association’s 7 scientific meetings, or to promote the Association’s clinical care guidelines, scientific statements, and advisories. Collaborate with team members to review and select abstracts to promote, provide peer edits for colleagues’ news releases, develop talking points, key messages for research authors and/or experts for commentary and perspective. Lead development of news kits for one or more of our scientific meetings, which includes review and selection of abstracts for promotion; developing detailed news releases that include expert quotes/perspectives as well as research author perspectives,; producing or collaborating with other teams for all related news materials, which may include video interviews, talking points, key messages, FAQs and/or infographics. Work with the Senior Director and the Vice President on the traditional and social media, as well as Association-owned channels. Develop strategic communications plans, media opportunities and relationships to promote the Association’s role as a thought leader in cardiovascular science and brain health, including the Association’s clinical care guidelines, scientific statements and advisories. Monitor the traditional media and social media landscape to ensure the Association can respond appropriately to breaking news related to heart and brain health and latest evidence-based recommendations to mitigate risk, as well efforts to protect the Association’s reputation and integrity. Collaborate with internal teams, including Science and Medicine, Science Operations, Scientific Publishing, Science Marketing, Social Media Marketing, Health and Science Programs, and Enterprise-Wide Mobilization teams, and external collaborators to optimize communications reach and amplify the Association’s life-saving mission among volunteers, internal stakeholders, and external partners. Supervise up to 2 members of the Science Media Relations team in close collaboration with the Senior Director. Lead or support other Communications initiatives as applicable and relevant. Mentor and coach Science Media Relations team members and internal and external collaborators. Want to help get your resume to the top? Five (5) years of excellent writing and editing skills, translating scientific research for the public, and solid knowledge of AP Style. Five (5) years of managing the submission of press, promotional, or related content, building relationships with journalists, and securing quality earned media coverage. Five (5) years of proficient computer skills, including all Microsoft Office programs, especially Word, PowerPoint, and Excel. Five (5) years of project management experience, including managing multiple projects concurrently. Five (5) years of demonstrated ability to work under tight deadlines, while facing competing demands and priorities for multiple projects. Ability to travel up to 10%-15% local and overnight stay. Preferred Qualifications: Eight (8) years of relevant experience. At least three (3) years of experience in a successful supervisory role. Proven ability to review and translate scientific abstracts and manuscripts; develop newsworthy ideas and approaches; write and pitch stories to media outlets; manage media interviews and produce news conferences, including prepping research authors and experts; craft talking points and/or key messages; foster collaborative relationships with reporters that position the organization as a primary resource for their stories. Portfolio demonstrating successful expertise in developing and implementing multi-faceted media strategies that generate visibility for scientific publications, journals, and scientific meetings. Company Overview At FUJIFILM Holdings America Corporation, we’re redefining innovation across the industries we touch—from healthcare and photography to semiconductors and data storage. With roots in photosensitive materials and a legacy of groundbreaking technology, we now lead 23 diverse affiliate businesses across the Americas. We’re looking for mission-driven talents eager to join us to help create, market, and support a vast portfolio of products. At Fujifilm you’ll have the opportunity to explore and grow your skills in new, exciting ways. Whether you’re shaping tomorrow’s tech or redefining today’s processes, we’ll provide a flexible work environment and dynamic culture where innovation thrives. Our Americas HQ is nestled in Valhalla, New York, a charming town known for its excellent schools, beautiful parks, and easy access to the vibrancy of New York City. Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit: Job Description Key Responsibilities Employee Communications Develop and execute integrated employee communication strategies aligned with business objectives, Corporate Communications Strategy, company culture, and organizational priorities. Partner with senior leaders and functional teams to develop clear, timely, and engaging communications for employees. Create and manage communications across multiple channels, including email, intranet, digital platforms, employee meetings, town halls, videos, newsletters, presentations, and leadership communications. Develop select executive communications, including talking points, leadership messages, presentations, town hall materials, and employee announcements. Translate complex business information into concise, accessible, and compelling employee communications. Support communications related to organizational change, business transformation, culture, employee engagement, and significant company initiatives. Establish communication plans, timelines, audiences, messages, and channels for major initiatives. Monitor employee feedback and engagement trends and recommend communications strategies based on employee needs and business priorities. Community Engagement Develop and implement community engagement strategies that support the company’s corporate citizenship and community investment priorities. Partner with business leaders, employees, nonprofit organizations, and community partners to identify meaningful engagement opportunities. Lead communications supporting volunteerism, charitable giving, employee-led community initiatives, and corporate social responsibility programs. Develop stories and content that demonstrate the company’s impact in local communities. Coordinate community events, employee volunteer activities, and engagement campaigns. Build relationships with internal and external stakeholders to increase employee participation in community initiatives. Measure and communicate the impact of community engagement programs. Content & Storytelling Develop compelling employee and community stories that reinforce company values, culture, Purpose, and business priorities. Write and edit articles, newsletters, executive messages, presentations, social content, videos, and other communications materials. Identify employee and community stories that can be leveraged across internal and external channels within FUJIFILM Americas, as well as amplified globally. Ensure communications are consistent with the company’s brand, voice, tone, and communication standards. Collaborate with social media, digital, HR, and external agency partners as appropriate. Strategic Partnership & Leadership Support Serve as a trusted, strategic communications advisor to leaders and cross-functional partners. Counsel stakeholders on communication strategy, audience considerations, timing, messaging, and delivery. Build strong relationships across the organization and understand business priorities and employee needs. Provide communications support during organizational changes, business milestones, and other high-priority initiatives. Manage multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining quality, accuracy, and deadlines. Required Skills/Education Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, or a related field. 10-12+ years of progressive experience in corporate communications, employee communications, public relations, community engagement, or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience developing and executing employee communication strategies. Excellent writing, editing, presentation, and verbal communication skills. Experience working directly with senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders. Strong project management and organizational skills. Ability to manage sensitive and confidential information with discretion. Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a complex, matrixed organization. Experience developing communications for multiple audiences and communication channels. Preferred Qualifications Experience in a global or large corporate environment. Experience supporting organizational change and employee engagement initiatives. Experience with community relations, corporate social responsibility, employee volunteerism, or charitable giving programs. Experience with executive communications. Experience with internal digital communications platforms, intranets, employee apps, or collaboration tools. Experience using employee engagement data, surveys, analytics, or other measures to inform communications strategy. Communications agency experience is a plus. Core Competencies Strategic Communications - Understands business objectives and translates them into effective communications strategies. Executive Partnership - Builds credibility and trusted relationships with senior leaders and provides thoughtful communications counsel. Writing & Storytelling - Creates clear, concise, compelling communications that connect with employees and community audiences. Stakeholder Management - Effectively collaborates with leaders and partners across functions, geographies, and levels of the organization. Employee Engagement - Understands employee audiences and develops communications that build connection, trust, understanding, and participation. Community Engagement - Builds meaningful partnerships and creates opportunities for employees and the company to positively engage with communities. Project Management - Effectively manages multiple priorities, deadlines, stakeholders, and deliverables. Judgment & Discretion - Demonstrates sound judgment when managing sensitive information, complex issues, and high-visibility communications. Success Measures Success in this role may be measured through: Employee engagement and participation in communications and community initiatives. Quality, reach, and effectiveness of employee communications. Stakeholder and leadership satisfaction. Successful execution of communications strategies and major initiatives. Employee understanding of key business priorities and organizational changes. Growth in employee participation in volunteerism and community engagement. Quality and consistency of communications across channels. Demonstrated community impact and stakeholder relationships. Role Characteristics The Employee Communications & Community Engagement Manager is a strategic individual contributor and communications partner who operates with a high degree of independence. The position requires the ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on execution and to work effectively with senior leaders, Fujifilm Americas Corporate Communications Leadership, employees, HR, and community partners. The role is particularly important in helping the organization connect employees to the company’s purpose, strategy, culture, and communities through credible, timely, and engaging communications. input.description: Senior Manager, Events Management Let’s be unstoppable together! Our predictive analytics and Liquid Data® platform help clients measure market share, uncover consumer behavior, and drive growth—powered by six decades of expertise and an expansive, high-quality data set. Learn more at Position Overview The Senior Manager, Events Management is responsible for planning and executing corporate meetings, conferences, client events, and strategic programs. This role independently manages assigned event programs and key workstreams, ensuring operational excellence and successful delivery against established event strategies. Reporting to the Senior Director II, Events Management, this role plays a key part in registration management, vendor coordination, onsite support, and post-event follow-up. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and service-driven, with hands-on experience managing corporate events from planning through execution. This individual will help strengthen event processes and operational rigor while delivering exceptional experiences for attendees, clients, and stakeholders. Key Responsibilities: Event Strategy & Program Management Manage the planning and execution of assigned meetings, conferences, incentive programs, and corporate events aligned to established business objectives and event strategies. Develop comprehensive project plans, timelines, communication strategies, and execution frameworks to support successful event delivery. Partner with business stakeholders and cross-functional teams to support event objectives, attendee experience requirements, and successful execution. Recommend process improvements, identify operational efficiencies, and contribute to implementing event management best practices. Apply industry best practices to help strengthen event processes, operational rigor, and consistency across programs and workstreams. Venue, Hotel & Destination Management Work with the Senior Director to manage room block administration, housing coordination, attendee accommodations, and related reporting. Collaborate to manage venue operations, including space planning, meeting room layouts, food and beverage requirements, signage plans, transportation logistics, and accessibility considerations. Support venue sourcing activities and assist with contract review, negotiation, and supplier management processes. Review and manage event deliverables, including rooming lists, Banquet Event Orders (BEOs), and venue specifications, to support successful event execution. Work with destination partners, convention and visitors' bureaus, and hospitality providers to enhance attendee experiences and optimize event outcomes. Budget Management & Financial Oversight Manage approved event budgets and ensure spending aligns with established financial guidelines, while maintaining exceptional attendee experiences. Monitor event expenditures, forecast costs, track budget variances, and identify opportunities for cost savings and operational efficiencies. Oversee invoice processing, contract compliance, and financial reconciliation processes to ensure accuracy and timely reporting. Prepare budget updates, variance reporting, and reconciliation summaries for leadership review. Onsite Event Leadership Support onsite event operations as part of a broader event team, exercising sound judgment on routine operational matters and escalating significant business, financial, legal, or reputational risks as appropriate. Coordinate vendors, contractors, temporary staff, and onsite resources to support flawless event execution and achievement of event objectives. Manage VIP and executive experiences, speaker logistics, crisis response, and real-time issue resolution. Maintain composure and sound decision-making in fast-paced environments while navigating changing priorities and unexpected event challenges. Ensure compliance with safety protocols, risk management standards, and organizational policies during all event activities. Team Collaboration & Growth Collaborate effectively with cross-functional partners. Support events and team members as needed during peak periods. Demonstrate a willingness to learn and grow within your role. Share event management best practices and contribute to the continued development of team capabilities and operational standards. Requirements Bachelor's degree in Event Management, Hospitality, Marketing, Communications, Business Administration, or a related field; equivalent professional experience considered. 4-6+ years of progressive experience managing corporate meetings, conferences, incentive programs, or experiential events. Demonstrated success managing multiple events simultaneously, including ownership of event logistics, budgets, vendors, and onsite execution. Experience with venue sourcing, contract negotiation, housing management, registration management, supplier management, and event procurement processes. Financial acumen with experience developing, managing, and reconciling event budgets. Proficiency with event technology platforms, including Cvent, registration systems, mobile event applications, reporting tools, and related event technologies. Strong project management, organizational, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder-management skills. Demonstrated ability to remain composed, adaptable, and solution-oriented while managing competing priorities in fast-paced, high-visibility environments. Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally as needed to support event execution, including occasional evenings and weekends. Must possess a valid passport, or be eligible and legally authorized to obtain one for international business travel. Circana Behaviors Beyond technical skills, experience, and role-specific attributes, these shared behaviors are fundamental to our culture and success. We seek individuals who consistently demonstrate and champion these behaviors in their daily work: Stay Curious: Being hungry to learn and grow, always asking the big questions. Seek Clarity: Embracing complexity to create clarity and inspire action. Own the Outcome: Being accountable for decisions and taking ownership of our choices. Center on the Client: Relentlessly adding value for our customers. Be a Challenger: Never complacent, always striving for continuous improvement. Champion Inclusivity: Fostering trust in relationships engaging with empathy, respect, and integrity. Commit to each other: Contributing to making Circana a great place to work for everyone. Location This position can be located remotely within the U.S . and must be able to work primarily within Central or Eastern Time business hours. Candidates located in the Chicago, IL area are strongly preferred, but location is not required. This role requires domestic and international travel to support onsite event execution. Candidates must possess a valid passport or be eligible and legally authorized to travel internationally for business purposes. The below range reflects the range of possible compensation for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, shift, travel requirements, sales or revenue-based metrics, any collective bargaining agreements, and business or organizational needs.
