input.title: Events Coordinator

organization.name: Preservation Society of Charleston
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: The Preservation Society of Charleston (PSC) is a member-supported nonprofit organization dedicated to preserving and protecting the historic character, quality of life, and cultural heritage of Charleston and its surrounding areas. Through advocacy, education, and community engagement, the Preservation Society serves as a trusted preservation resource for residents and visitors alike. A dynamic calendar of member-exclusive events, public programs, tours, workshops, and volunteer opportunities is central to fulfilling this mission. The Events Coordinator supports the planning and execution of these experiences, helping create meaningful opportunities for people to connect with Charleston's history and the work of historic preservation. Reporting to the Director of Programs and Learning, this position plays a key role in delivering exceptional experiences by coordinating event logistics, assisting attendees, managing registrations, and supporting event operations before, during, and after programs. In addition, this position provides field support to the Communications and Advancement teams by capturing photos and gathering content during events and programs, ensuring timely documentation and sharing of materials for use in marketing, publications, and social media. Job Duties: • Monitor ticket sales and registrations, maintain event records, and support accurate tracking systems, programs, and special events. • Assist the Director of Programs and Learning and Advancement staff with day-of setup, event logistics, and breakdown. • Provide exceptional customer service and professional communication to members, volunteers, event attendees, partners, and the public. • Answer the events phone line and email, respond to event questions, assist attendees with ticket purchases, and troubleshoot ticketing issues. • Coordinate check-in, including preparing attendee lists, assisting late arrivals, and communicating with registrants as needed. • Assist with volunteer support for the Fall Tours, including answering questions, distributing materials and supplies, and helping ensure volunteers have what they need to be successful. • Attend internal and external meetings as deemed necessary or as assigned, and work as a team with all departments at PSC. • Capture and organize photos, participant stories, and program highlights during events, and provide timely content and information for use in publications, newsletters, website updates, and social media. • Assist with outreach to community partners, vendors, and rental inquiries as assigned. • Attend community and networking events as necessary to build relationships and promote the PSC. Knowledge and Experience: Required Qualifications • Excellent customer service skills • Strong written and verbal communication • Excellent organizational skills • Ability to maintain neat and structured staging areas on or off-site • Ability to work independently and as part of a team • Proficiency with Microsoft Office including Word, Outlook, and SharePoint • This is an in-person position requiring regular attendance at the Preservation Society of Charleston office and at programs and events throughout the year. Remote work is minimally available for this role. Preferred Qualifications • Experience coordinating events, educational programs, or tours • Experience with customer service, hospitality, museums, nonprofits, or public-facing programs • Knowledge or interest in historic preservation and Charleston history • Experience using EveryAction, ticketing platforms, registration systems, or similar databases Skills and Abilities: • Serve as a positive ambassador for the Preservation Society of Charleston, demonstrating professionalism, courtesy, and enthusiasm for the organization's mission. • Highly organized, proactive, and able to anticipate needs, prioritize tasks, and manage multiple assignments simultaneously. • Flexible, adaptable, and able to thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced environment while also working independently. • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build positive working relationships across departments, with volunteers, members, and the public. • Demonstrate sound judgment, professionalism, and a commitment to high ethical standards. Physical Requirements: The position requires the ability to move throughout event spaces, often outdoors and at historic properties, for extended periods; frequently bend, lift up to 40–50 lbs.; and visually monitor event sites. The role balances active, physical demands during events with periods of computer-based planning and administrative work. Transportation: A personal vehicle is required for this position, as travel between event sites throughout the Charleston area is frequently necessary. Mileage reimbursement is provided for approved work-related travel in accordance with the Preservation Society's reimbursement policy. Schedule: Full time, Exempt. Irregular hours are required, including some evenings and weekends for events. Compensation: $44,000-$47,000, commensurate with experience Benefits: 15 days annual paid vacation leave 6 days annual paid sick leave 11 annual paid holidays Company-matched retirement plan Group health, vision, and dental insurance plans Generous professional development opportunities Paid parking EEO Statement: Preservation Society of Charleston is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an equitable and inclusive environment for all employees. Applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status. TO APPLY: Please submit a cover letter and resume to our Director of Finance and Operations, Amanda Coté with Events Coordinator in the subject line: acote@preservationsociety.org. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis. Early applications are encouraged. No phone calls, please.

input.description: Description Spoleto Festival USA is internationally recognized as America's premier performing arts festival. For 17 days and nights each spring, Spoleto Festival USA fills Charleston's historic theaters, churches, and outdoor spaces with performances in opera; theater; dance; and chamber, symphonic, choral, and jazz music. Spoleto Festival USA is a 501(c)(3) charitable organization. The Venues Venue Coordinators are situated at two extraordinary venues in Charleston, South Carolina: 14G and Festival Hall. These dynamic and versatile venues offer indoor and outdoor space that can accommodate a wide range of events and occasions, and are managed and operated by Spoleto Festival USA. The Role Venue Coordinators are the face of Spoleto Festival USA at 14G and Festival Hall. This role owns the onsite experience for every client, vendor, and guest who comes through the door, and is also responsible for the safety, security, and condition of the facility during the shift. Venue Coordinators most often work solo onsite with no other Spoleto staff present, so we're looking for someone proactive, trustworthy, and comfortable exercising independent judgment, handling conflict gracefully, and solving problems on the spot. At Spoleto, nothing is ever "usual," so not only do you have to be willing to roll up your sleeves and get things done, but you have to be willing to have fun doing it. Please note, Venue Coordinators are generally not scheduled during our Festival season in the months of May and June. Most shifts occur between July and April. Position Type: Hourly, non-exempt, part-time/intermittent, not benefit-eligible Hours: Not guaranteed; on average, Venue Coordinators work one to two events a month, and shifts are yours to choose Anticipated Start Date: There is no specific anticipated start date, as we are continually seeking qualified candidates Location: Charleston, SC (onsite) - 14G and Festival Hall Department: Operations Reports to: Operations Manager What You'll Do Serve as the primary onsite point of contact for clients, vendors, and guests, most often working independently without other staff present. Collaborate with event organizers, clients, and vendors to ensure flawless event execution. Oversee setup, breakdown, and organization of event spaces, and open and close the venue as required. Conduct pre- and post-event inspections to keep the venue clean, well-maintained, and ready for use. Maintain a professional, welcoming demeanor with clients, guests, and vendors, and resolve concerns in real time, exercising sound, independent judgment. Monitor event activities for compliance with venue policies and safety regulations, and serve as the primary onsite point of contact for emergency response. Assist with crowd control and other event-day logistics. Help maintain inventory of event supplies and equipment, and complete event and incident reports as needed. What You'll Bring Prior experience in a customer-facing role such as events, hospitality, or retail. Demonstrated ability to work independently and exercise sound, on-the-spot judgment. Trustworthy and reliable, comfortable serving as the sole onsite representative during a shift. Experience navigating and de-escalating conflict, and resolving unexpected issues in real time. A proactive, self-starting approach; you anticipate needs and address them before they become problems. Ability to work well under pressure and adapt to changing event dynamics, with strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Basic knowledge of event setup and audiovisual equipment operation. A positive, service-first attitude. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams) and comfort learning new tools. Requirements Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S.; this employer participates in E-Verify. Must be able to pass a background check. Must be comfortable and able to access high grid spaces and work at height, including on catwalks, ladders, and stairs. Must be comfortable working in low light or no light environments and in confined spaces, with exposure to the elements and loud noise. Requires standing for long periods, lifting up to 50 lbs., and moving/pulling/pushing up to 100 lbs. with assistance if necessary. Most shifts occur on nights, holidays, and weekends, and require extended hours; Venue Coordinators are generally not scheduled during the Festival season (May-June). Based on-site in Charleston, SC, at 14G and Festival Hall. Compensation The hourly rate for this position is $18.00 per hour. This is a part-time, intermittent/as-needed role and is not eligible for Spoleto Festival USA's full-time benefits package. We're accepting and reviewing applications on a rolling basis, so please don't be discouraged if you don't hear from us right away. We appreciate your interest and patience. Spoleto Festival USA is an equal opportunity employer and committed to diversity in hiring. Spoleto Festival USA does not discriminate in employment on the basis of an individual's race, color, sex, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, hairstyles or hair texture, national origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, parental status, marital status, military status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law. Our greatest strength comes from our ability to come together as unique individuals - come as you are and bring the best version of yourself. Uncertain if you fulfill every requirement? Don't let that deter you. We enthusiastically evaluate a wide spectrum of candidates and welcome you to apply. If you need an accommodation to complete the application process, please contact us at careers@spoletousa.org.

Passion for social media, visual storytelling, and staying ahead of industry trends. Please include a portfolio or portfolio link with your application. Job Overview Unrivaled is seeking an experienced independent videographer to provide video production services in support of its basketball clubs during the 2026–2027 Unrivaled season. The engagement is expected to begin on December 14, 2026, with onsite production activities in Miami, Florida beginning on or around December 26, 2026, and continuing through approximately mid-March 2027, subject to completion of the agreed scope of services. Except where onsite attendance is reasonably required for games, events, shoots, or other production activities, the contractor will determine how and where to perform the services necessary to complete the agreed deliverables. Key Responsibilities Provide videography and editing services for original content, including player features, social media series, branded content, and behind-the-scenes storytelling. Coordinate with Content, Social, and other creative contributors to develop creative concepts and execute approved projects from pre-production through final delivery. Capture high-quality video footage at games, practices, league events, studio productions, and off-court shoots. Edit and deliver video content optimized for multiple distribution channels, including TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, broadcast, partner channels, and other designated platforms. input.description: Leveling the Fields is a programs-focused nonprofit dedicated to increasing the number of girls in sports, recognizing the strong correlation between sports participation and future leadership roles. We are committed to breaking down barriers and providing universal access to sports, regardless of financial constraints, geographical limitations, or lack of options. Through our EmpowerPlay and PlayFit programs, we aim to get more girls into sports, keep them engaged, and equip them with the tools needed to thrive as future leaders. EmpowerPlay The EmpowerPlay Program is a dynamic multi-sport after-school program aimed at empowering girls through athletics and is designed specifically for girls in 3rd through 5th grade. The program is run onsite at the elementary school. Over the nine weeks, participants learn the fundamentals of each sport while building teamwork and confidence. Our program is designed to foster self-acceptance, positive body image, and good sportsmanship through our unique empowerment journal. For girls in low-income areas, the program is offered at no cost to families. PlayFit The PlayFit Enrichment Program is a weekly add-on designed to complement existing after-school programs, offering a fun and engaging way for 3rd-5th grade girls to stay active and build confidence. The program focuses on a single sport, allowing participants to deepen their skills, and is available in a 6-week or 8-week format. With on-site coaching and equipment provided, PlayFit makes it easy for girls to explore sports and develop teamwork and leadership skills. Designed to be accessible for all, this program brings empowerment and physical activity directly to your after-school care. , Volunteer Role Video Editor Organization Leveling the Fields Reports to Marketing Chair Time Commitment 3 to 6 hours per week (flexible) Role Overview The Video Editor is responsible for turning raw photo and video footage from our programs into polished, short-form videos for social media, email, and fundraising. This role helps bring our programs to life through clear, engaging storytelling. This role will oversee YouTube content and/or social media videos. Key Responsibilities Edit short-form videos using provided footage (reels, clips, highlights) Create content optimized for social media and digital use Apply basic branding (logos, text overlays, music, pacing) Organize and export final assets to shared folders Collaborate with the Marketing Chair on priorities and deadlines Ideal Fit Comfortable editing video (CapCut, Premiere Pro, Final Cut, Canva, or similar) Strong sense of pacing and storytelling Reliable, detail-oriented, and able to meet light weekly deadlines Passion for youth sports and community impact Why This Matters Your edits help showcase the confidence, growth, and joy happening on the field—and make our impact visible to supporters and partners.

input.description: Leveling the Fields is a programs-focused nonprofit dedicated to increasing the number of girls in sports, recognizing the strong correlation between sports participation and future leadership roles. We are committed to breaking down barriers and providing universal access to sports, regardless of financial constraints, geographical limitations, or lack of options. Through our EmpowerPlay and PlayFit programs, we aim to get more girls into sports, keep them engaged, and equip them with the tools needed to thrive as future leaders. EmpowerPlay The EmpowerPlay Program is a dynamic multi-sport after-school program aimed at empowering girls through athletics and is designed specifically for girls in 3rd through 5th grade. The program is run onsite at the elementary school. Over the nine weeks, participants learn the fundamentals of each sport while building teamwork and confidence. Our program is designed to foster self-acceptance, positive body image, and good sportsmanship through our unique empowerment journal. For girls in low-income areas, the program is offered at no cost to families. PlayFit The PlayFit Enrichment Program is a weekly add-on designed to complement existing after-school programs, offering a fun and engaging way for 3rd-5th grade girls to stay active and build confidence. The program focuses on a single sport, allowing participants to deepen their skills, and is available in a 6-week or 8-week format. With on-site coaching and equipment provided, PlayFit makes it easy for girls to explore sports and develop teamwork and leadership skills. Designed to be accessible for all, this program brings empowerment and physical activity directly to your after-school care. , Event Coordinator (Volunteer) Organization Leveling the Fields Commitment 5 Hours a week, planning for 4-6 events per year Reports to Marketing Committee Chair Works Closely With Marketing and Operations Teams Position Overview The Volunteer Event Manager is responsible for planning, organizing, and coordinating fundraising, community outreach, and special events that support the mission of the organization. This volunteer leadership role works closely with staff, board members, volunteers, sponsors, and community partners to ensure successful events that engage participants, raise awareness, and generate support for the nonprofit. Key Responsibilities Event Planning and Coordination Develop event plans, timelines, budgets, and logistical requirements. Coordinate all aspects of events, including venue selection, registration, catering, equipment, entertainment, and event setup. Ensure events align with the organization's mission, goals, and budget constraints. Manage event schedules and monitor progress toward milestones. Volunteer and Team Management Recruit and train event volunteers (recruitment efforts will be supported by Volunteer Manager) Delegate responsibilities and provide guidance before and during events. Facilitate volunteer meetings and event briefings. Promote a positive and collaborative volunteer experience. Marketing and Promotion Collaborate with marketing content team to promote events through social media, email campaigns, and community outreach. Collaborate with marketing content team to develop promotional materials Encourage participation from supporters, donors, and community members. Event Execution Oversee event operations on the day of the event. Serve as the primary point of contact for volunteers, vendors, and participants. Address issues and make decisions to ensure smooth event operations. Ensure compliance with safety and organizational policies. Evaluation and Reporting Collect feedback from participants, volunteers, and stakeholders. Evaluate event outcomes against established goals. Prepare post-event summaries, including attendance, fundraising results, lessons learned, and recommendations for future events. Qualifications Strong organizational and project management skills. Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities. Experience planning events, fundraising activities, or community programs preferred. Ability to lead and motivate volunteers. Problem-solving skills and attention to detail. Ability to work independently and collaboratively. Commitment to the mission and values of the organization. Time Commitment Approximately 5–10 hours per week, with additional time required leading up to and during major events. Flexible scheduling, including occasional evenings and weekends. Benefits Of Volunteering Opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the community. Develop leadership, event management, and nonprofit experience. Build professional and community networks. Contribute directly to the success and growth of the organization. Performance Expectations Success in this role will be measured by Effective planning and execution of events. Achievement of attendance and fundraising goals. Positive volunteer and participant experiences. Timely completion of event-related tasks and reporting. Strong collaboration with staff, board members, and community partners.
